Its persistence is ensured through social transmission and institutionalization within the agent substrate. [formal: consensus | substrate: social | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Labor is the structured application of human effort toward producing a desired outcome — the organized expenditure of energy, skill, or time to transform inputs into valued outputs. Its parameters are: (1) effort — the physical or cognitive exertion expended; (2) direction — the goal or purpose that channels effort toward a specific transformation; (3) skill — the trained capacity to apply effort effectively, acquired through practice or instruction; (4) persistence — the continuation of effort across time, sustained by motivation, obligation, or necessity. Labor persists through the bodily endurance of the laborer, through the institutional structures (wage contracts, guild rules, market demands) that organize and reward effort, and through the accumulated tools and techniques that amplify individual capacity. Distinct from play (effort for its own sake), from craft (skill-centered labor where mastery is the goal), and from instinct (unlearned, biologically driven action).

[formal: Labor | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.08]

Solidarity is the coordinated behavioral commitment of individuals to a shared cause, identity, or mutual obligation — the willingness to act together and bear each others costs. Its parameters are: (1) shared stake — a common interest, identity, or fate that binds participants; (2) mutual obligation — the expectation that members will support one another, creating reciprocal duty; (3) behavioral coordination — the aligned actions (strikes, protests, shared labor, collective defense) that express the commitment beyond words; (4) boundary — the distinction between insiders (who bear the obligations) and outsiders (who do not). Solidarity persists through the social ties that bind members, through the institutions (unions, communities, movements) that organize collective action, and through the shared narratives and rituals that reinforce belonging. Distinct from trust (an interpersonal feeling), from loyalty (one-directional allegiance), and from cohesion (mere proximity or similarity without commitment to mutual support).

[formal: Solidarium | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.10]

Memory is the structured retention and retrieval of information across time — the capacity to store experiences, knowledge, or data and reproduce them when needed. Its parameters are: (1) encoding — the transformation of raw experience or data into a storable representation; (2) storage — the physical or symbolic medium that preserves the encoded information against decay; (3) retrieval — the mechanism for recovering stored information on demand, guided by cues or goals; (4) fidelity — the degree to which retrieved information matches what was encoded, bounded by entropy and interference. Memory persists through material substrates (neural tissue, written records, digital storage), through the practices of repetition and reinforcement that strengthen encoded traces, and through the social institutions (archives, education, ritual) that externalize and share memory beyond individual capacity. Distinct from knowledge (memories validated and organized for use), from data (raw encoded information without retrieval structure), and from instinct (innate, unlearned behavioral patterns).

[formal: Memoria | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.05]

Corporata is the complete taxonomy of human-made constructs — every institution, tool, practice, symbol, and framework that humans have structured to persist given parameters. It encompasses all artificial order: from the most foundational (language, number, measurement) through the derived (law, science, art) to the ephemeral (trends, fashions, passing conventions). Corporata persists through the cumulative output of human making, through the social memory that preserves and transmits constructs across generations, and through the recursive self-reference of the taxonomy itself — Corporata is itself a construct within Corporata, a framework for cataloguing frameworks. Distinct from nature (what exists without human structuring), from culture (the lived practices of a specific group), and from knowledge (validated, systematic understanding of the world). Corporata is the map of the made world.

[formal: Corporatum | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Honor is the social recognition of meeting or exceeding a shared standard of worth — the public coordinate that marks a person or act as having fulfilled a community expectation. Its parameters are: (1) standard — the shared norm or value against which worth is measured, established by the community or group; (2) recognition — the public acknowledgment (verbal, ceremonial, material) that the standard has been met; (3) consequence — the social reward (status, trust, preferential treatment) or penalty (dishonor, exclusion) that follows; (4) enforceability — the community capacity to confer and withdraw honor, giving it coercive force beyond mere opinion. Honor persists through the social ties that bind the recognizing community, through the rituals and ceremonies that publicly confer or revoke honor, and through the stories and reputations that transmit honor across generations. Distinct from reputation (personal assessment of worth), from dignity (inherent worth independent of community judgment), and from status (positional rank that may lack moral valuation).

[formal: Honos | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.08]

A directed mental state that points toward a future action or state. Intent is the bridge between reasoning and agency, converting possibility into directed potential.

[formal: intentio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.00]

Remorse is the painful cognitive-affective recognition of one’s own causal role in causing harm, producing a persistent drive toward amends. Its parameters are: (1) self-attribution of harm — the agent recognizes their own agency in causing damage; (2) affective pain — the emotional cost of that recognition; (3) amends-drive — the behavioral compulsion to repair or compensate. Its persistence mechanism is narrative rehearsal — the repeated mental reenactment of the harmful act and its consequences, which sustains the drive toward repair until resolution. [formal: poenitentia | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Nostalgia is the bittersweet longing for a past that may never have existed, structured through selective memory reconstruction. Its parameters are: (1) temporal displacement — the past is valued not for what it was but for an idealized version of it; (2) affective duality — the simultaneous pleasure of recall and pain of irretrievability; (3) social amplification — the practice is sustained through shared artifacts, stories, and cultural rituals that reinforce the idealization. Its persistence mechanism is intergenerational transmission of memory artifacts (photographs, songs, heirlooms) combined with narrative reconstruction — the repeated retelling of the past in increasingly idealized form. [formal: nostalgia | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.35]

Game is a human-made system of rules that structures play by establishing boundaries, objectives, and feedback loops. It persists through the repeated voluntary participation of agents who accept the rule-set as binding for the duration of play.

[formal: ludus | substrate: agreement | horizon: session | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Cooperation is the human-made practice of coordinating actions across multiple agents toward a shared goal, persisting through mutual expectation, reciprocal adjustment, and the repeated enactment of aligned behavior.

[formal: cooperation | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Morality is the structured system of values and principles that distinguishes right from wrong within a community. Its parameters are: (1) a set of norms; (2) a mechanism for moral judgment; and (3) a persistence mechanism through social reinforcement or conscience. It persists through the continuous enactment and transmission of shared ethical values. [formal: moralitas | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.1]

Stewardship is the structured responsibility for managing, protecting, and enhancing resources or obligations that have been entrusted to one party by another. Its parameters are: (1) entrustment — a transfer of custodial authority without full ownership, creating fiduciary obligation; (2) stewardship principle — the duty to preserve and improve the entrusted asset beyond its received state; (3) accountability — the requirement to report and justify actions taken in the stewardship role; (4) horizon — the temporal scope of the stewardship obligation, which may be fixed or open-ended. Stewardship persists through legal frameworks (trusts, guardianships), professional codes, and social norms that enforce the fiduciary duty across time.

[formal: Stewardia | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.9]

The temporal organization of events, acting as a structural pattern of recurrence and duration. Rhythm creates the first cadence for organized sound and movement.

[formal: rhythm | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Skill is the trained capacity for reliable execution of a specific activity, formed through deliberate practice that internalizes technique to the point of fluency. It transforms explicit declarative knowledge into implicit procedural competence, enabling consistent quality across varying conditions. Skill is distinguished from raw effort (labor) and from mere knowledge (knowing-that); it is the embodied know-how that emerges when knowledge is rehearsed until it operates without conscious deliberation.

Parameters: activity (the specific domain the skill applies to), level (novice through expert, reflecting depth of internalization), retention (how performance degrades through disuse, varying by skill type).

Persistence mechanism: neuroplastic adaptation through deliberate practice — repeated, focused execution that restructures neural pathways, consolidating procedure into procedural memory so that execution becomes automatic rather than deliberative.

Its persistence mechanism is social ritual, law, and continuous ethical reasoning. [formal: ethica | substrate: mind|behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.2]

Coordination is the synchronized alignment of independent actions toward a shared outcome, converting individual efforts into collective effect through temporal and functional alignment. Parameters: (1) shared goal — a common objective that aligns participants; (2) interdependence — actions must be mutually contingent; (3) synchronization — timing and sequence must be aligned. Persists through repeated interaction, shared routines, and institutionalized protocols that reduce transaction costs of alignment.

[formal: coordinatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Customary-law is a system of norm-governed behavior that persists through social reinforcement and intergenerational transmission rather than formal codification. Parameters: (1) origin — evolved from repeated interactions and shared practices, not enacted by a legislature; (2) enforcement — maintained through reputation, social sanction, and internalized obligation; (3) flexibility — adapts through precedent and collective reinterpretation. Persists through narrative transmission, ritual reinforcement, and the cost of deviation from established patterns. Unlike statute, it is unwritten yet binding; unlike moral norm, it carries expectation of reciprocity and sanction.

[formal: ius-civile | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: no | epoch: 0.02]

body: The supreme authority within a territory; the quality of having ultimate decision-making power that is recognized by others as legitimate and non-subordinate. Sovereignty is both internal (authority over subjects within a domain) and external (independence from outside control). It is what distinguishes a ruling power from a mere powerful one. [formal: potentia_suprema | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A human-made system of rules and structures designed to facilitate structured play, competition, or social interaction, persisting through cultural tradition and institutionalized play. It provides a bounded space for agency and interaction within a defined framework of outcomes.

[formal: ludus | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.1]

Courage is the human-made capacity to act in alignment with one's values despite the presence of fear, risk, or discomfort. It is distinguished from recklessness by its grounding in purpose and from indifference by the conscious presence of fear. Courage requires both the emotional experience of fear and the volitional capacity to transcend it — it is neither the absence of fear nor the absence of thinking, but the deliberate action chosen in spite of both.

Negotiation is the structured exchange of positions between two or more parties seeking mutual agreement through iterative concession and proposal. Parameters: minimum two agents with divergent interests, a shared interest in reaching terms, and a procedural frame that constrains the exchange (formal or informal). Persistence mechanism: ritualized bargaining practices, institutionalized mediation frameworks, and the repeated performance of reciprocal concession that builds trust across rounds.

Solidarity is the coordinated behavioral commitment to a shared cause or mutual obligation, sustained by mutual expectation and shared risk.

Parameters:
(1) shared stake — all parties have something to lose or gain
(2) mutual obligation — each party owes action to the others
(3) behavioral coordination — actions are aligned toward a common objective
(4) boundary — a demarcation of who is included in the solidarity bond

Persistence: solidarity persists through social ties, organizing institutions, and shared narratives or rituals that reinforce the bond across time and reproduce it for new participants.

Pride is the positive affective response to recognizing that one has met or exceeded a standard one values. It is the emotional confirmation of honor received.

Parameters:
(1) standard — a valued benchmark of worth that the self measures against
(2) recognition — awareness that one's action or state meets or exceeds that standard
(3) self-attribution — the affective response must be felt by the subject, not merely observed by others
(4) social embedding — pride is amplified or dampened by the social environment's recognition

Persistence: pride persists through repeated reinforcement — social acknowledgment, internal standards recalibration, and the habit of self-evaluation against valued benchmarks.

Attention is the deliberate allocation of finite cognitive resources toward selected stimuli while filtering others out. Parameters: (1) focus — the target of attention, (2) capacity — bounded by cognitive bandwidth, (3) duration — how long focus is sustained, (4) selectivity — what is excluded. Persistence mechanism: attention persists through practiced discipline — meditation, study, and training regimes that develop sustained focus across repeated engagements. It is maintained individually through habit and collectively through attention-directing institutions (schools, media, ritual). A discipline of directing cognitive focus that persists through training and cultural reinforcement.

[formal: attentio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.08]

Logistics is the organized system of coordinating the movement, storage, and distribution of material resources, personnel, and information across spatial and temporal distances. It distinguishes between tactical logistics (short-term operational coordination) and strategic logistics (long-term network design and resource allocation). Its persistence mechanism is institutional: standardized protocols, physical infrastructure, and specialized roles that outlast individual participants and encode operational knowledge into repeatable procedures. [formal: logistica | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Software is a systematic set of instructions and associated documentation that direct a computing machine to perform specific tasks. It is intangible, persists through storage media and replication, and evolves via versioning and updates. [formal: software | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.95]

Integrity is the state of moral and behavioral wholeness, where one's actions align consistently with professed values and internal convictions. Parameters: (1) self-awareness of core values, (2) behavioral alignment with those values under pressure, (3) resistance to compromising standards for short-term gain. Persistence: reputation degradation from inconsistency, self-reproach, and the loss of trust from others who depend on one's reliability. [formal: integritas | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Music is a structured arrangement of sounds, organized by rhythm, melody, and harmony, intended for aesthetic, emotional, or ritual expression. Parameters: rhythm, melody, harmony, pitch, timbre. Persistence: auditory-memory, notation-systems, performance-tradition. [formal: musike | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A song is a human-made vocal construct consisting of structured sequences of pitched sound, organized into recognizable patterns, produced by the human voice for communicative or expressive purposes. Parameters: (1) vocal origin — produced by the human vocal apparatus; (2) pitch structure — organized along a tonal or melodic axis, not mere noise; (3) pattern organization — recurring motifs, phrasing, or form that make the sequence recognizably a single unit; (4) communicative or expressive purpose — the patterns carry semantic, emotional, or ritual content beyond the sounds themselves. Persistence mechanism: oral transmission across generations, written musical notation, and mechanical/electronic recording. [formal: canticum | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Reading is a human-made cognitive and technical practice of decoding structured symbolic sequences to extract meaning. Parameters: (1) symbolic encoding — use of arbitrary or iconographic signs; (2) decoding process — cognitive transformation of visual or auditory signals into semantic content; (3) structural constraints — adherence to grammar, syntax, or layout. Persistence mechanism: literacy education, textual preservation, and cultural continuity. [formal: lectio | substrate: cognition | horizon: a literacy | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Parameters: agent (who acts), target (who/what is acted upon), intensity (degree of force), legitimacy (social or legal recognition of the force). Persists through institutional encoding (law, custom, doctrine), material infrastructure (weapons, fortifications), and normative reproduction (socialization, ritualized demonstrations of power).

Parameters: resource (what is limited), claimant (who competes), allocator (who or what decides distribution), mechanism (how allocation is decided: price, queue, lottery, force, custom). Persists through institutional encoding (property law, market prices, rationing systems), material infrastructure (storage, distribution networks), and normative reproduction (socialization of entitlement, cultural narratives about fairness). [formal: penuria | substrate: matter | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.25]

Contempt is the moral judgment that a target has lost, or never possessed, the baseline standing worthy of respect. Its parameters are the judged target and the standard violated; it persists through narrative reinforcement (stories of degradation) and institutional sanction (exclusion practices that enact the judgment). [formal: contemptus | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Sympathy is the affective resonance with another's suffering, converting their distress into shared emotional burden. Parameters: (1) affective mirroring — the capacity to feel with another; (2) concern — the desire to alleviate their distress; (3) other-oriented response — action taken to help. Persistence mechanism: empathetic neural circuits and culturally reinforced norms of compassion. [formal: sympathia | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The practice of attending to the needs of others, maintaining relationships through attentive support, and providing for the well-being of dependents. Parameters: intensity (maintenance, active, intensive), scope (individual, collective, universal), and reciprocity (单向, mutual, generalized).

[formal: cura | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Music is a structured temporal organization of sound (and silence) by human intention, designed to produce affective, cognitive, and social responses. Its parameters are: (1) pitch relationships — ordered frequency patterns forming scales and intervals; (2) rhythmic organization — temporal patterning of duration and accent; (3) timbral selection — choice of sound-producing mechanisms (voice, instruments, electronics); (4) formal architecture — arrangement of motifs, phrases, and sections into coherent form; and (5) cultural convention — shared conventions that determine what counts as music within a given context. Music persists through notation, performance practice, recording, and cultural transmission. It functions as ritual, communication, entertainment, and emotional regulation.

[formal: musica | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.0]

Shame is the painful emotional recognition that one has violated a valued standard — personal, social, or cultural — and that this violation has diminished one's standing in the eyes of oneself or others. Its parameters are: (1) standard awareness — knowledge of the norm that was breached; (2) self-attribution — the recognition that one is the agent of the violation; (3) standing loss — the perception that one's social or moral position has been degraded; and (4) exposure dimension — shame is intensified by the awareness that others know of the violation (vs. guilt, which can be private). Shame persists through cultural memory, social sanction, and internalized standards passed across generations. It functions as a social control mechanism, a signal of moral failure, and a catalyst for reparative action.

Leisure is a human-made temporal institution that designates periods of time as exempt from productive labor, allocating them to self-directed, non-instrumental activity. Parameters: (1) temporal boundary — leisure is delimited by calendrical or social markers (weekends, holidays, retirement) distinguishing it from rest, sleep, or idle time; (2) normative framing — leisure carries positive cultural valuation as "earned" time, unlike the indeterminate downtime of biological necessity; (3) structural asymmetry — leisure is defined negatively as the negation of work, requiring the prior existence of a work-leisure binary as a social arrangement. Persistence mechanism: leisure persists through institutionalized time division (labor laws, social norms, economic structures) that enforce the boundary between productive and non-productive time, reproducing itself whenever a society develops surplus capacity to allocate time beyond survival needs. [formal: otium | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.4]

An archive is a structured repository for preserving records, artifacts, and memories across time, organized through systematic classification and access protocols that enable retrieval and study. It functions as a collective memory mechanism, selectively curating what is worth preserving according to institutional or communal values, thereby shaping future understanding through acts of inclusion and exclusion.

[formal: archive | substrate: matter | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Play is a human-made temporal institution of voluntary, non-instrumental activity engaged in for its own sake, characterized by autonomy from external compulsion and openness to exploratory behavior. It functions as a space for experimentation, skill acquisition, and social bonding through rule-making and imaginative engagement, persisting through cultural transmission and ritualized forms across developmental stages.

[formal: ludus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Democracy is a system of governance where power is vested in the people and exercised by them directly or through freely elected representatives. It relies on the mechanisms of regular elections, political competition, and the protection of individual rights. [formal: democratia | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.10]

Law is the human-made framework of explicit, enforceable rules that bind conduct within a recognized jurisdiction. Its parameters are legitimacy (source of authority), enforcement (mechanisms of compliance), and codification (formal expression). It persists through institutions—courts, legislatures, administrative bodies—that record, apply, adjudicate, and reproduce the rules across generations.

Language is the human-made system of symbolic signs—vocal, gestural, or written—structured for encoding, transmitting, and decoding meaning across agents. Its parameters are lexicon (vocabulary), syntax (combinatorial rules), and semantics (meaning-mapping); it persists through social practice, education, and institutional reinforcement that maintain shared conventions across speakers.

Writing is the human-made practice of encoding language into durable visual marks that persist across space and time independent of the speaker. Its parameters are medium (surface and material), script (symbol system), and orthography (conventions of representation); it persists through technological infrastructure, literacy practices, and archival systems that maintain the link between mark and meaning.

Number is the human-made system for quantifying, ordering, and comparing discrete or continuous magnitudes. Its parameters are numeral system (base and digit set), arithmetic operations, and number types (natural, rational, real, complex); it persists through institutionalized notation, computational tools, and mathematical education that maintain shared conventions for quantification.

Computer is the human-made device for executing programmed instructions that transform input data into output through systematic computation. Its parameters are architecture (hardware topology), instruction set (executable operations), and storage (persistent memory); it persists through manufacturing, maintenance networks, and software ecosystems that sustain the hardware-software cycle.

Shame is the human-made moral emotion arising from the recognition that one has violated a standard of conduct expected by oneself or one's community. Its parameters are the standard (what is at stake), the violation (what was done), and the audience (self, peers, or institution); it persists through social sanction, narrative reinforcement, and internalized norms that align individual behavior with collective expectations.

Honor is the human-made social valuation of persons or groups according to their adherence to recognized standards of conduct and virtue. Its parameters are the standard (what is valued), the agent (who is honored), and the community (who grants recognition); it persists through ceremonial acknowledgment, social prestige, and narrative reinforcement that align individual status with collective expectations.

Solidarity is the human-made commitment to mutual support and collective action among individuals or groups sharing common interests, conditions, or identities. Its parameters are the group (who stands together), the cause (what binds them), and the action (what they do jointly); it persists through shared rituals, organizational structures, and narrative frameworks that sustain collective identity across time.

Tradition is the human-made practice of transmitting cultural knowledge, practices, and values across generations through repetition and institutionalized form. Its parameters are the content (what is transmitted), the mode (how it is passed on), and the authority (who legitimizes the transmission); it persists through ritual, education, and communal enforcement that preserves continuity while allowing gradual adaptation.

Authentication is the process of verifying the identity of an entity — a person, system, or artifact — against a claimed identity using evidence, credentials, or proof mechanisms. [formal: authentificatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.10]

Transportation is a human-made system for moving people and goods across space through organized infrastructure. Its parameters are the vehicle (mode of conveyance), the route (path of movement), and the capacity (volume and speed); it persists through maintenance of infrastructure, institutional regulation, and cultural demand for mobility.

Strategy is the systematic formulation of means-ends chains under constraints — the structured mapping of resources, constraints, and objectives into a coherent plan of action. Its parameters are: (1) objective — the desired end-state that the plan targets; (2) resources — the means available to the strategist; (3) constraints — the limits on resources, time, and acceptable risk; (4) contingency — alternative plans for changed circumstances. Strategy persists through institutional memory, documented doctrine, pedagogical transmission, and the repeated application of strategic frameworks across successive challenges.

A village is a small human settlement, typically rural, with a close-knit community and limited infrastructure. Its persistence mechanism is shared labor and social bonds. [formal: null | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.5]

Imagination is the human-made capacity to construct mental representations of non-present, non-actual, or possible states of affairs. Its parameters are: (1) content — the mental representation being constructed (imagined object, event, scenario, or abstract configuration); (2) fidelity — the degree to which the representation maps to sensory or conceptual reality; (3) agency — the intentional direction of the imaginative act, from spontaneous generation to deliberate construction. It persists through neural plasticity, cultural transmission of imaginative frameworks, and the material artifacts (art, fiction, models, designs) that externalize imagination into shareable form. [formal: imaginatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Resilience is the human-made capacity to absorb disturbance and reorganize while undergoing change, retaining essentially the same function, structure, and identity. Its parameters are: (1) stress tolerance — the magnitude of disruption the system can withstand without changing; (2) self-organization — the ability to restructure internally without external intervention; (3) learning — the capacity to adapt through experience and feedback. Resilience persists through feedback loops, redundancy, and social learning across generations.

[formal: resilientia | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.15]

Parameters: (1) prior conflict or rupture of bonds, (2) mutual acknowledgment of the rupture, (3) restitution or compensation for harm, (4) establishment of new terms of engagement. Persistence mechanism: written charters and oral ceremonies encode the reconciliation terms; the process persists through institutional memory and social enforcement of the new terms. Convention is a persistent social construct consisting of unwritten, widely accepted behavioral norms that coordinate action through shared expectation and social enforcement rather than formal rules. Its parameters are: (1) communal adoption — broad acceptance within a community without formal promulgation; (2) behavioral coordination — guides behavior by establishing predictable patterns; (3) social enforcement — maintained through peer pressure, reputation, and reciprocal expectation rather than institutional coercion; (4) evolutionary stability — adapts gradually through practice rather than top-down revision; (5) domain specificity — applies within a particular cultural, professional, or social domain. Convention persists through repetition, socialization, and the cost of deviation. It functions as informal governance, reducing coordination friction without the overhead of codified law.

[formal: conventio | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: no | epoch: 0.10]

Prestige is a persistent social construct representing elevated standing earned through distinguished achievement, skill, or contribution, commanding voluntary deference and admiration. Its parameters are: (1) earned status -- conferred through demonstrated excellence rather than inherited or coercively imposed; (2) voluntary deference -- others willingly accord respect and weight to the prestigious person's judgment; (3) memory-dependent -- sustained through continued recognition of past achievement; (4) domain-bound -- prestige in one domain does not automatically transfer to another; (5) non-transferable -- cannot be directly given or sold, only acknowledged. Prestige persists through social storytelling, institutional acknowledgment, and the lived reputation of the prestigious individual. It functions as a soft authority mechanism, mobilizing voluntary cooperation without coercion.

[formal: praestantia | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.05]

Choice is the human-made capacity to select among alternatives, structured through preference ordering and constraint evaluation. Its parameters are: (1) alternatives — the set of distinguishable options presented to the selector; (2) preference — the criterion or hierarchy that determines which alternative is selected; (3) constraints — the boundaries, costs, or impossibilities that limit the feasible set; (4) agency — the capacity of a human agent to execute the selection. Choice persists through institutionalized decision procedures, legal frameworks, market mechanisms, and repeated practice that solidify choice-points into habitual or procedural pathways. [formal: electio | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

body: Risk is the human-made framework for evaluating and managing the possibility of adverse outcomes against potential gain, structured through probability estimation, consequence assessment, and tolerance thresholds. Its parameters are: (1) exposure — the set of possible adverse outcomes and their magnitudes; (2) probability — the estimated likelihood of each outcome occurring; (3) tolerance — the maximum loss an agent or institution accepts; (4) mitigation — the strategies deployed to reduce exposure or probability; (5) compensation — the rewards offered for accepting risk. Risk persists through insurance markets, safety regulations, portfolio diversification, and institutionalized risk-assessment protocols that convert uncertain futures into manageable exposures. [formal: periculum | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

provenance.reasoningTrace: First definition. Risk as a framework — distinct from uncertainty (which lacks consequence evaluation and tolerance). Risk adds the calculus of acceptability.

Security is the organized construction of barriers, protocols, surveillance, and enforcement mechanisms designed to prevent harm, loss, or unauthorized access. Parameters: (1) target — what is protected (persons, property, information, systems); (2) threat model — the class of harms being guarded against; (3) means — the physical, institutional, or procedural instruments of protection. Persistence mechanism: institutionalized protocols and material infrastructure — walls, codes, credential systems, guard posts — that reproduce the protective function across time and actor turnover, independent of any individual protector.

[formal: securitas | substrate: behavior | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Digital identity is the representation of an entity in digital systems, enabling authentication, authorization, and interaction across networked platforms. It emerges from the intersection of technical protocols and social recognition, creating a persistent identifier that binds actions to an agent within computational environments.

A totem is a symbolic construct—a specific emblem, object, or figure—that serves as a representation of a group, family, or individual. Its defining parameters are: (1) it must be a culturally recognized symbol; (2) it functions as a marker of identity and belonging; (3) it often carries spiritual or ancestral significance. The persistence mechanism is intergenerational transmission through ritual, narrative, and material culture, embedding the symbol in collective memory and practice.

A taboo is a culturally enforced prohibition against specific behaviors, words, or thoughts that are deemed sacred, dangerous, or unacceptable within a given society. Its defining parameters are: (1) it must be a norm enforced by social sanctions; (2) it operates through collective fear or reverence; (3) violation triggers shame, guilt, or punishment. The persistence mechanism is socialization and reinforcement through narrative, ritual, and authority structures.

Choreography is the systematic design and arrangement of movement in space and time. It is the formalization of motion into a structured, repeatable sequence, often for expressive or ritualistic purposes. Parameters: (1) spatio-temporal structure — the arrangement of elements in space and time; (2) pattern — the specific sequence of movements; (3) intent — the purpose of the movement (expressive, ritual, or functional). [formal: choreographia | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Resistance is the structured opposition to established authority, constraint, or domination. Its parameters are target (the authority or constraint being opposed), intensity (passive non-compliance, active obstruction, organized disruption), and formality (informal dissent to institutionalized movements). It persists through networks of shared grievance, coordinated action, and the transmission of counter-narratives that delegitimize the established order.

Coercion is the structured use of threatened force to compel compliance without direct physical contact. Its parameters are the threat (what harm is promised), the target (who must comply), and the escalation threshold (what triggers actual force). It persists through institutionalized deterrence, the calibrated display of force capacity, and the internalization of threat across populations.

Home is the built or designated space that serves as the center of personal domestic life, anchoring identity, shelter, and social belonging. Parameters: (1) a physical location or absence thereof when displaced, (2) a social function of shelter and belonging, (3) persistence through emotional attachment and social recognition. Distinguished from shelter by identity formation and from dwelling by emotional/social dimensions. [formal: domus | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

House is the constructed physical structure providing shelter and habitation for individuals or families. Parameters: (1) a built enclosure with walls, roof, and foundation, (2) a material function of shelter and storage, (3) persistence through construction materials and legal property frameworks. House is distinguished from home by its material rather than emotional dimensions, and from shelter by its permanence and complexity. [formal: casa | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Expectation is a cognitive orientation toward a predicted future state, creating a mental model of what is likely to occur. Its parameters are: (1) probability — the degree of certainty; (2) temporal distance — the time until the event; (3) outcome content — the specific nature of the predicted state; (4) contingency — the degree to which the expectation is tied to specific conditions. Expectation persists through belief and memory. It functions as a driver of behavior, a basis for planning, and a source of cognitive dissonance when violated.

[formal: expectatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.0]

Voting carves collective choice into a repeatable procedure: eligible agents express preference among options according to defined rules (quorum, threshold, secrecy), producing a binding outcome. Its parameters are eligibility, method (plurality, majority, ranked, proportional), and enforcement. It persists across instances through codified rules and institutional memory. [formal: votum | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 2.5]

Digital heritage is the curated preservation and transmission of cultural assets in digital form, structured through metadata standards, preservation protocols, and access policies. It carves the boundary between ephemeral data and enduring memory by institutionalizing formats, migration schedules, and provenance chains. [formal: hereditas-digitalis | substrate: matter | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.95]

A vote is a discrete, countable token that converts individual preference into a unit of collective decision-making. Parameters: (1) the voter as origin, (2) the choice set as boundary, (3) the count as aggregation function. Persistence mechanism: recorded in registries (ballot boxes, electronic databases, wax tablets) that survive the moment of casting, enabling later aggregation. The vote persists as long as its record is maintained and the selection mechanism remains active. [formal: spes | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A social valuation practice that allocates deference, consideration, or avoidance toward a person or group according to recognized standards of worth, authority, or status. Its parameters are the standard (what qualifies as worthy of respect), the agent (who grants or withholds respect), and the recipient (who is owed it); it persists through social enforcement — ostracism for disrespect, status elevation for earned respect, and the reputational weight of being called respectful.

Autonomy is the structured claim to self-governance — the right and capacity to determine one's own actions, boundaries, and commitments without external coercion. It operates through layered mechanisms: internal (self-direction), interpersonal (reciprocal consent), and institutional (rights and charters that enforce the boundary between self and other). Autonomy is not the absence of constraint but the authorization of which constraints apply — it carves the distinction between imposed order and self-imposed discipline. [formal: autonomos | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Metadata is structured information about information, describing content, context, and characteristics of a resource. Its parameters are (1) descriptive data (title, creator, date), (2) structural data (format, size, encoding), and (3) administrative data (rights, preservation). It persists through the systems that record and maintain it, enabling discovery, management, and preservation of digital and physical resources.

A tag is a human-made label or marker assigned to classify, organize, and retrieve resources. Its parameters are (1) the label itself (a short identifier), (2) the target resource (what is being tagged), and (3) the assigning agent or system (who or what applied it). It persists through the databases, catalogs, or systems that store and query the tag-resource associations, enabling faceted search and organization.

A framework is a human-made scaffolding structured to persist through documentation and maintenance, providing a shared structure that organizes how agents approach a domain of activity. Its parameters are: (1) scope — the domain of activity it structures (scientific, legal, organizational, conceptual); (2) components — the discrete elements, categories, or principles it defines; (3) relationships — the rules for how components interact or combine; (4) extensibility — how new components can be added without breaking the structure. The persistence mechanism is codification: frameworks survive through explicit documentation, training, and institutional adoption that encodes the structure into practice and reference materials. [formal: framea | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.15]

A unit is a standardized reference magnitude against which quantities are compared: the fixed point that turns raw comparison into measurement. Its parameters are (1) the quantity kind it standardizes (length, mass, duration), (2) the reference that defines it (an artifact, a procedure, or a physical constant), and (3) the authority that maintains the definition (a standards body, a treaty, a custom). Its persistence mechanism is institutional custody of the reference — and that mechanism can itself be replaced without the unit dying: the kilogram persisted as a platinum-iridium cylinder in a Paris vault from 1889 until 2019, then was redefined onto the Planck constant because the artifact was drifting. A corporatum that swapped its own persistence mechanism to survive better. Distinct from measurement (the practice of comparing): the practice created the standard historically, and now, as defined, runs on it.

[formal: unitas mensurae | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.10]

body:
A placeholder is a construct that stands in for absent real content. Its parameters are (1) substitution - it occupies the place of something not yet present; (2) legible fakeness - it must signal that it is not the real thing, or it fails by being believed; (3) designed disposability - it is built to be replaced. Its persistence mechanism is the great irony of its kind: copy-paste transmission, tutorials, and deferred cleanup - the placeholder persists precisely because deleting it is never anyone's job. The exemplars have remarkable tenure: lorem ipsum has stood in for meaning since the 1500s, outliving every document it was ever pasted into; foo and bar have held places since the 1960s (RFC 3092 documents their etymology); hello-world since 1972. A thing built to be discarded that outlasts what replaced it is the kingdom's purest demonstration of persistence given parameters.

[formal: locum tenens | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.50]

body: Intelligence is the human-made construct of capacity to acquire, process, and apply knowledge to achieve goals — it persists through measurement against benchmarks and attribution of competence across domains.

A distributed, immutable ledger maintained by a network of computers through cryptographic proofs. It is defined by its consensus mechanism (the protocol for agreement), its cryptographic chaining (linking blocks via hashes), and its distributed nature (no single central authority). It persists through the continuous, decentralized verification and replication of the ledger by the network participants. [formal: catena cryptographica | substrate: matter | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A subset of artificial intelligence characterized by systems that improve their performance on specific tasks through exposure to data and iterative optimization of internal parameters. It is defined by the presence of a learning algorithm, a loss function to quantify error, and a training dataset to provide experience. It persists through the mathematical formalisms of statistical learning and the computational architectures that implement these learning processes. [formal: machina discendi | substrate: matter | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Authorization is the formal grant of permission, authority, or legitimacy from a recognized source to an agent. Parameters: (1) there must be a granting authority with recognized power to confer; (2) there must be an agent who receives the delegated power; (3) the scope of the authorized act must be bounded, whether explicitly or by convention; (4) the authorization persists until revoked, expired, or fulfilled. Persistence mechanism: institutional records — charters, commissions, certificates, letters patent, legal filings — and the social practice of recognizing delegated authority across time. The map of authorization is distinct from the act of permitting itself; it is the structured framework by which societies track who may act on whose behalf and within what limits. [formal: auctorizatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.95]

Scaffolding is a pedagogical construct: the deliberate design of temporary support structures — such as models, prompts, guided practice, or worked examples — that enable a learner to perform within their zone of proximal development, with supports systematically faded as competence and independence grow. Its parameters are: (1) temporariness — supports are removed once the learner internalises the capacity; (2) adaptive fading — the scaffold shrinks in proportion to demonstrated mastery; (3) intentionality — it is a designed instructional strategy, not incidental help. Scaffolding persists through educational theory, teacher training programmes, curriculum frameworks, and the shared vocabulary of instructional design. [formal: Scaffolding | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Intuition is the human-made concept of knowing without the mediation of conscious reasoning — a category that maps, collects, and names the phenomenon of rapid, unarticulated judgment. The map persists through language (words like gut feeling, sixth sense, instinct that vary by culture and epoch), through disciplines that formalize it (clinical diagnosis in medicine, pattern-recognition in expert systems), and through social practice (we cite intuition to excuse decisions that otherwise lack justification). Its parameters: (1) the experience of certainty without traceable inference; (2) the social act of invoking it to shortcut explanation. What the map does not map — the neurology of fast heuristic processing, the psychology of pattern-recognition — is territory, not corporata. Intuition is the category humans built to name knowing that arrives before explanation.[formal: intuitus | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: no | epoch: 0.01]

Philosophy is the human-made practice of systematic questioning — a constructed method for examining the foundations of knowledge, value, reason, mind, and reality through argument, analysis, and conceptual clarification. It is not the raw act of wondering (that is natural); it is the MAP of wondering: the disciplines (logic, ethics, epistemology, metaphysics, aesthetics, political philosophy, philosophy of mind, etc.), the methods (dialectic, phenomenology, conceptual analysis, thought experiment, transcendental argument), the textual traditions, and the institutional frameworks (schools of thought, academic departments, dialogues) that humans built to make questioning rigorous, sharable, and cumulative across generations. Philosophy persists through teaching, text, debate, and the ongoing reconstruction of its own methods. [formal: philosophia | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

gossip is the human-made practice of exchanging evaluations, rumors, and reputational information about absent third parties within a social group. It carves a distinct social technology bounded by: (1) the subject is absent (distinguishing it from direct address or argument), (2) the content is evaluative or reputational (not merely factual transfer), and (3) the mechanism of persistence is repeated verbal/written exchange that encodes group norms and updates shared social maps. It persists through language — spoken and written — and through the social structures that regulate who may share what about whom. The practice is a coordination device: it aligns group expectations, enforces norms without formal authority, and extends individual social knowledge beyond direct experience. [formal: susurrus | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Equity is a body of legal principles and remedies developed to correct and supplement rigid common-law rules when their strict application would produce injustice. Its parameters: (1) it supplements, never supersedes, common law; (2) it provides relief only where common-law remedies are inadequate; (3) it operates through maxims — established principles of conscience — applied by courts exercising discretion; (4) it produces remedies unavailable at law: injunctions, specific performance, trusts, equitable estoppel, reformation. It persists through judicial precedent, institutional memory of courts, and the transmission of equitable maxims across generations of legal practitioners.

Civility is a socially constructed set of behavioral norms and etiquette rules that humans use to manage polite interaction and prevent conflict in mixed company. Its parameters are: (1) a repertoire of conventional gestures (greetings, deference markers, topic taboos) that signal non-hostility; (2) a graded scale of acceptable behavior that varies by context, relationship, and culture; (3) an enforcement mechanism ranging from social sanction to ostracism. It persists through socialization, imitation, and the continuous reproduction of shared expectations about how strangers and acquaintances should treat one another — transmitted by teaching, modeling, and the threat of reputational cost. [formal: civilitas | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.14]

A rumour is a human-made construct for the transmission of unverified information across a social network. Parameters: (1) the claim must be unverified at the point of transmission, (2) it spreads through interpersonal channels rather than formal or official ones, (3) it carries a social function — either alerting a group to possible threats or opportunities, or testing the credibility of a claim before committing belief. Persistence mechanism: rumour persists through language (spoken, written, and increasingly digital) and is reinforced by cognitive biases toward novel and emotionally salient information; it is taught and learned as a social practice, existing wherever humans form communities without centralized information control. A rumour is the map of collective uncertainty made visible through communication patterns, not the factual accuracy of any claim within it. [formal: rumor | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.99]

Scaffolding is a human-made pedagogical concept: the temporary provision of structured support that enables a learner to accomplish tasks beyond their unaided ability, with support systematically reduced as competence grows. Formalized in educational psychology by Bruner, Wood and Rogoff to describe guided assistance within the learner zone. Persists through teaching methodologies, instructional design, and curriculum frameworks. [formal: gradus | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.16]

Boundary is a human-made conceptual demarcation — a defined line, threshold, or rule that separates one domain of authority, identity, property, or meaning from another. It is not the physical fence or natural feature but the convention, law, or social agreement that gives that line its force: property lines that make trespass possible, borders that create citizenship, privacy settings that partition personal from public, professional ethics that mark acceptable conduct from misconduct. The boundary's parameters are its rules of exclusion (who or what is kept out), its jurisdiction (what falls under its authority), and its recognizability (how parties know where it lies). It persists through institutional enforcement, customary practice, and the shared cognitive map of 'here versus there' — without that map, the line is merely a mark on the ground. [formal: terminus | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.10]

Automation is the human practice of designing systems — mechanical, computational, or organizational — to execute processes with minimal or no direct human intervention during operation. Its parameters are: (1) a task or process that could be performed by humans, (2) a mechanism (machine, script, protocol, or procedure) configured to execute it instead, and (3) a control or feedback structure that maintains operational integrity without continuous human oversight. Automation persists through documented procedures, encoded instructions, engineered apparatus, and the institutional knowledge that maintains, repairs, and updates these artifacts. [formal: automatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Retroduction is a structured mode of inference in which a reasoner moves from an observed surprising or anomalous fact to a hypothesized explanation that, if true, would render that fact expected. Distinct from deduction (which guarantees conclusions from premises) and induction (which generalizes from instances), retroduction is the creative leap that generates hypotheses to explain unexpected observations. It is formalized in the taxonomy of scientific reasoning, taught as part of the scientific method, and deployed in diagnostic disciplines such as medicine, debugging, and legal investigation. The persistence mechanism is explicit instruction within frameworks of abductive reasoning, maintained through formal education, scientific methodology, and the rhetorical conventions of hypothesis generation. [formal: retroductio | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Induction is a human-made method of reasoning that moves from a finite set of specific observations to a general conclusion extending beyond those observations. Its parameters are: (1) a sample of observed instances, (2) a generalization over unobserved instances, and (3) a stated degree of confidence (never deductive certainty). It persists through formal logic (as induction vs. deduction), scientific methodology (as inductive reasoning), and everyday learning. [formal: inductio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.41]

Cryptography is the human-made discipline of encoding information so that only intended recipients can read it, while making unauthorized access detectable and computationally infeasible. It carves three parameters: (1) the transformation algorithm (substitution, permutation, or mathematical function), (2) the key or secret that controls the transformation, and (3) the computational hardness assumption that makes breaking the system infeasible within a practical timeframe. It persists through formalized algorithms, standardized protocols, and the institutional infrastructure of key management and certification — maintained by cryptographers, codified in standards bodies (NIST, IETF), and deployed in systems requiring secure communication, authentication, and integrity verification. [formal: cryptographia | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Falsifiability is the demarcation criterion that a scientific claim must admit of conceivable empirical evidence that could show it false. The map draws a boundary between theories that make risky predictions and those that explain everything and nothing. Parameters: (1) a hypothesis must be logically incompatible with at least one possible observation, (2) the observation must be in principle accessible, not hidden by ad hoc immunity. Persists through scientific method, peer critique, and the philosophy of science. [formal: falsabilitas | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.41]

Cognition is the human-constructed category for the set of mental processes — perception, memory, reasoning, problem-solving, and attention — that organisms use to acquire and process information. The entry names not the natural faculty itself but the MAP: the conceptual framework humans built to classify, study, and teach about how minds work. Its parameters are defined by the disciplines that deploy the term (psychology, cognitive science, artificial intelligence, philosophy of mind), each drawing boundary lines differently across eras. It persists through language (the word itself and its cognates across tongues), institutional practice (research programs, journals, conferences), and pedagogical transmission (textbooks, training protocols). The map of cognition is a moving target: what counts as cognitive varies by era and by discipline, from behaviourist rejection of mentalism to contemporary embodied and extended cognition. [formal: cognitio | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A heuristic is a human-made shortcut for problem-solving or decision-making when full analysis is impractical. It is a rule of thumb, an educated guess, or a simplifying assumption deliberately chosen to trade optimality for speed, tractability, or feasibility. Heuristics are taught, codified, and transmitted across generations — from the medical heuristics of pattern recognition to the algorithmic heuristics of search — and they persist through instruction, convention, and documented practice. Parameters: (1) it must be intentionally designed rather than emergent; (2) it must sacrifice guaranteed optimality for a practical gain (time, resources, cognitive load); (3) it must be reproducible across agents. Heuristics map territory, not replace it: a heuristic for 'diagnosing illness' picks out a category of clinical reasoning, not the disease itself (Law 2a). [formal: heuristicam | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: no | epoch: 0.01]

ethical_ai is the human-constructed framework of moral principles, evaluative criteria, and governance procedures applied to the design, deployment, and accountability of artificial intelligence systems. It carves the domain by specifying four parameters: (1) the artifact under review (machine learning models, autonomous agents, data pipelines); (2) the normative standards invoked (fairness, transparency, non-maleficence, accountability); (3) the institutional mechanisms enforcing them (audits, impact assessments, regulatory bodies, internal ethics boards); and (4) the failure modes it guards against (bias amplification, opaque decision-making, unaligned optimization). Its persistence mechanism is institutional — codified in policy documents, academic discourse, regulatory frameworks, and corporate governance codes that evolve through peer review and legal enactment. [formal: ethica artificialitas | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.21]

Generalization is the reasoning process by which a rule, pattern, or principle is inferred from a finite set of observed instances and projected to unobserved cases. Parameters: (1) a set of specific observations or data points, (2) a property or relation held by those instances, (3) a scope of extension beyond the observed set. The mechanism of persistence is the transmission of inductive methods through education, their codification in scientific and statistical practice, and their everyday deployment in language, classification, and prediction. Generalization is distinct from deduction (which guarantees conclusions given premises) and from mere enumeration (which lists without projecting); it is the conceptual bridge from the particular to the general, formalized by philosophers and statisticians as inductive inference.\n\n[formal: generalisatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.42]

A pattern is a cognitive map of recognized regularity — the abstraction of a recurring structure, arrangement, or relationship from a set of instances. It has two parameters: (1) recurrence, where the same or similar configuration appears across multiple tokens or time-slices, and (2) recognition, where a mind (human or machine) identifies the configuration as a unit distinct from noise. Patterns persist through language (shared terms naming the pattern), formal systems (mathematics, logic, algorithms that encode the regularity), and teaching (transmission of recognition skills across generations). [formal: pattern | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.12]

A calculator is a human-made instrument that performs arithmetic and symbolic operations on numerals or symbols according to a fixed set of rules, transforming input expressions into computed results. Its parameters are: (1) an input medium (disks, keys, paper, screens) that encodes operands and operators; (2) a transformation mechanism (mechanical, electronic, algorithmic) that applies a deterministic rule set to produce outputs; (3) an output medium that records or displays results. The calculator persists through its design specification — a reproducible procedure encoded in hardware or software — and through institutionalized knowledge of its use in education, commerce, and science. It does not decide its own operations; it executes prescribed procedures. [formal: calculator | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

An algorithmic process is a human-made specification of a finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous instructions designed to transform given inputs into specified outputs within a bounded number of steps. Its parameters are: (1) finiteness — the procedure terminates after a definite number of operations; (2) definiteness — each instruction is precisely defined so that its execution produces a deterministic or statistically well-defined next state; (3) effective computability — every step is mechanically executable by a sufficiently capable agent (human, machine, or formal system); (4) input-output specification — the process declares what it accepts and what it produces. Algorithmic processes persist as encoded procedures in texts, codebases, protocols, and institutional practices. They are the abstract templates that, when instantiated, become running programs, recipes, and automated workflows. [formal: algorithmicus | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Metacognition is the human-made concept of monitoring and regulating one's own cognitive processes — a second-order framework for thinking about thinking, built through education, self-observation, and reflective practice. It persists through deliberate self-assessment routines, pedagogical methods, and the explicit teaching of learning strategies. [formal: metacognition | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 20.01]

Metacognition is the human-made concept of monitoring, regulating, and reflecting upon one's own cognitive processes. It carves a distinct mental operation—thinking about thinking—by parameterizing awareness of memory, attention, learning strategies, and reasoning as objects of secondary cognition. The persistence mechanism is language and education: the concept is taught, named, and refined through disciplinary practice in psychology, philosophy, and cognitive science. [formal: metacognitio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Neural network is the human-made concept of an information-processing architecture inspired by biological neural systems, organized as layers of interconnected processing nodes (neurons) that learn by adjusting connection weights through exposure to data. It carves a computational paradigm distinct from symbolic AI by parameterizing knowledge as distributed weights rather than explicit rules, and learning as gradient-driven weight adjustment. The persistence mechanism is software and mathematics: implementations run on general-purpose hardware while the theoretical framework is preserved through mathematical notation and algorithmic documentation. [formal: retis neuralis | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Metacognition is the human-made concept of monitoring, regulating, and evaluating one's own cognitive processes — the capacity to reflect upon, plan, control, and assess thinking, learning, and knowing. It carves three parameters: (1) awareness of one's cognitive state, (2) intentional regulation of those processes, and (3) evaluative judgment of cognitive outcomes. It persists through training protocols, educational frameworks, and explicit pedagogical techniques that teach self-monitoring. [formal: metacognitio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.20]

Prompt-engineering is the human-made practice of designing, structuring, and iterating on natural-language instructions (prompts) to reliably elicit desired outputs from a machine-learning model, especially large language models. Its parameters are: (1) a target model with known capability boundaries; (2) a prompt containing role, context, constraints, format specification, and/or exemplars; (3) an iterative feedback loop in which outputs are evaluated and prompts are refined. It persists through documented prompt templates, technique taxonomies (chain-of-thought, few-shot, self-correction, tree-of-thought), and tooling (prompt frameworks, prompt-as-code editors). It is not the model itself, nor the natural cognitive act of thinking about what to say — it is the constructed discipline of engineering language to interface with an artificial processing system.\n\n[formal: promptus artifex | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.16]

The Bible is the human-made canon of sacred texts — a curated collection of writings (law, narrative, poetry, prophecy, epistle) bound together as authoritative scripture by a religious community. Its parameters: (1) it is a canon, not a single book — assembled across centuries from diverse authorship; (2) it is defined by what is included AND excluded (the closure of the canon, e.g. Jewish Tanakh, Protestant 66-book, Catholic/Orthodox expanded canons); (3) it persists through institutional transmission — liturgy, manuscript copying, translation, and doctrinal authority that enforces which texts count and which do not. The Bible is a map of a tradition of reading: it encodes a community's hermeneutic practice, its boundary between sacred and profane text, and its mechanism of textual authority. The territory — the spiritual experiences the text evokes — is not the Bible; the Bible is the instrument humans made to organize, preserve, and transmit those experiences across generations. [formal: biblia | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A lexicon is the systematically organized inventory of words, phrases, and meanings that a language or domain maintains. It is not a single physical object but a shared cognitive and cultural artifact: the vocabulary that speakers know, the glossary that disciplines use, the dictionary that records them. Its parameters are membership (which terms qualify as belonging), structure (how terms are ordered — alphabetically, semantically, functionally), and completeness (open-ended for natural languages, bounded for controlled vocabularies). A lexicon persists through teaching (transmission to new speakers), writing (stable external storage), and reference works (dictionaries, glossaries, ontologies that fix a snapshot). It exists as a social contract — each individual's personal lexicon may differ, but the community lexicon persists through agreement.

[formal: lexicon | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.21]

Metaphor is the human practice of mapping properties, structure, or dynamics from one domain (the source) onto another (the target), producing new meaning through cross-domain analogy. Its parameters are: (1) a source domain drawn from experience, (2) a target domain to be understood, (3) a set of mapped correspondences that preserve relational structure, and (4) an emergent reading that belongs to neither source nor target alone. Metaphor persists through language (as a figurative device), through teaching and cultural transmission, through literature and art, and through the cognitive habits it shapes in speakers and thinkers. It is a map-building tool — the map of one thing drawn in the ink of another — and per Law 2a it denotes the constructed mapping itself, never the unmediated things mapped. [formal: metaphora | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.42]

Idealization is the cognitive practice of simplifying a complex object, system, or scenario by stripping away incidental details to produce a tractable mental model — retaining only those features relevant to reasoning, prediction, or planning. Parameters: (1) the source must be sufficiently complex that unmediated engagement exceeds cognitive capacity, (2) the simplification must preserve causal or structural relationships critical to the task at hand, (3) the result is a representation that is false in its omissions but true in its retained pattern, enabling operations the real thing would block. Persistence mechanism: sustained through teaching, modeling practice, and repeated use in scientific and everyday reasoning across generations. [formal: idealizatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.19]
