Persistence mechanism: the material substrate endures across time as a physical document; the erased text persists as ghost-writing recoverable through chemical, spectral, or digital imaging techniques. [formal: palimpsestum | substrate: matter | horizon: centuries | explicit: no | epoch: 0.01]

A bailiff is a court officer responsible for maintaining order, security, and procedural discipline within a courtroom and its surrounding facilities. Definition parameters: (1) appointed or elected officer of a court or legislative body; (2) duties include courtroom security, escorting jurors, maintaining silence, executing court orders; (3) acts as the agent of the court's authority in the physical space. Persistence mechanism: the role persists as an institutional position within the legal system — created by statute, custom, or court rule, filled by appointment or election, and sustained through the ongoing operation of the judicial institution it serves. [formal: baillivus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Mnemonic devices are human-made techniques and structures designed to extend and improve memory retention and recall. They operate by encoding information into more memorable forms — through visualization, association, chunking, rhythm, or spatial placement — exploiting the mind's natural propensity for patterns, images, and narratives over abstract data. Common forms include acronyms, the method of loci, rhymes, acrostics, and peg-word systems. Their persistence depends on teaching, practice, and cultural transmission: a mnemonic device exists as a construct only when encoded into human practice and transmitted across individuals. [formal: dispositio mnemonica | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.78]

A manuscript is a human-made handwritten or typewritten document that predates mechanical printing. It is produced by deliberate acts of inscription on physical substrates (parchment, paper, papyrus, tablets) by hand, distinguishing it from printed texts by the direct hand-authorship of every character. Its parameters: (1) produced by hand (not mechanically reproduced), (2) carries the author's or scribe's direct physical trace in letterforms, spacing, and corrections, (3) exists as a unique physical object or a small batch of authorially-controlled copies. It persists through physical preservation — archival storage, copying, and institutional custody — and through the cultural practice of valuing original authorial handwriting. A manuscript is distinguished from a printed book by the absence of a printing press intermediary; it is distinguished from a draft by its relative completeness as a text. [formal: manuscriptum | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.01]

Schemata (singular: schema) are structured frameworks of knowledge that humans use to organize, interpret, and store information. Parameters: (1) hierarchical organization — information is arranged in parent-child category relations; (2) default values — each schema carries expected properties for its members; (3) activation threshold — a schema becomes available for use when triggered by relevant cues. Persistence mechanism: schemata persist through language (naming and teaching category structures), through written documentation in cognitive science and philosophy, and through cultural transmission via educational practices that shape how individuals categorize experience. The construct is the map — the human-built taxonomy of schema types (scripts for events, frames for situations, stereotypes for social groups) — not the neural instantiation. [formal: schema | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A proviso is a limiting clause appended to a proposition, statute, contract term, or grant that carves out an exception, condition, or reservation from the general rule. Parameters: (1) it must attach to a parent proposition that it qualifies; (2) it introduces a condition whose truth value determines whether the parent proposition holds; (3) it operates as a defeasibility marker — the main claim stands unless the proviso's condition is triggered. Persistence mechanism: proviso structures endure through written legal instruments, contractual documentation, and legislative text, where they are preserved by the archival and citation infrastructure of law. [formal: proviso | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Self-testing is a cognitive learning strategy in which learners actively generate questions about study material and attempt to answer them without external cues, forcing retrieval practice and metacognitive monitoring of knowledge state. Parameters: (1) the learner must independently generate the test items (not merely respond to externally provided questions), (2) responses must be unaided retrieval (no reference to source material during recall), (3) the process must include a feedback phase where correct answers are compared against a knowledge standard. Persistence mechanism: sustained through instructional design (test-effective pedagogy), curriculum standards, teacher training programs, and the institutionalized practice of formative and summative assessment in educational systems. [formal: sebatatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.68]

Transfer-of-training is the educational construct describing how knowledge or skills acquired in one context become available in another. Parameters: (1) source domain where learning originally occurred, (2) target domain requiring application, (3) degree of similarity between domains (near transfer = similar structure, far transfer = superficially different but structurally parallel). Persistence mechanism: maintained through instructional design practices, assessment frameworks, and the scholarly literature of educational psychology that defines, measures, and theorizes transfer across contexts. [formal: translatio trainingi | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

errata-slip: A discrete correction notice distributed alongside a published document to rectify errors discovered after release. Parameters: (1) it lists specific corrections with page/line references; (2) it is physically or digitally distinct from the original document; (3) it carries an authoritative attribution (publisher, author, or editor). The persistence mechanism is institutional distribution — inserted into remaining stock, mailed to purchasers, or pushed as a digital update. Errata-slip exists because published artifacts are imperfect and human audiences expect corrections without rewriting the original. [formal: errata | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

recency-bias: The cognitive tendency to recall the most recently encountered items more accurately and vividly than earlier items in a sequence. Parameters: (1) operates within ordered sequences (lists, narratives, conversations); (2) the recency effect coexists with but is distinct from the primacy effect; (3) it is modulated by interference, delay, and attentional load. The persistence mechanism is neural encoding dynamics in working and episodic memory — recent items remain in a heightened state of accessibility. As a concept, recency-bias is the MAP of this memory phenomenon, deployed in psychology, behavioral economics, and decision science to explain systematic recall and judgment errors. [formal: recentia | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Self-regulated learning is a deliberate cognitive architecture that enables learners to direct their own learning through cyclical phases: (1) forethought — setting goals and planning strategies before engagement; (2) performance — executing strategies while monitoring progress; (3) self-reflection — evaluating outcomes and adjusting future approaches. The parameters that define it are: it must be a cyclic process, must involve conscious goal-setting, and must produce observable strategy adaptation. It persists through formal instruction in metacognitive strategies, through learning analytics platforms that feedback to learners, and through pedagogical training programs that teach the skill. [formal: auto-regulatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.80]

Clothing is a human-made artifact system: garments constructed from processed materials and worn on the body for coverage, protection, adornment, or status signaling. Parameters: (1) manufactured from transformed materials (fibers, leather, synthetics); (2) designed for human-body fit (cut, size, drape); (3) serves functional or symbolic purposes (weather shielding, modesty, identity, professional signaling). Persistence mechanism: industrial and artisanal manufacture chains, cultural transmission through fashion systems and retail, and material production infrastructure. Clothing is not merely fabric — it is shaped, sized, and coded by human convention.

A cognitive strategy is a deliberately designed mental procedure for improving how information is encoded, organized, retrieved, or evaluated. The concept covers techniques such as self-testing, elaborative interrogation, dual coding, and spaced practice — each is a method taught to learners so they can apply it to their own thinking. Parameters: (1) intentional — the learner chooses and deploys it; (2) procedural — it specifies a repeatable operation on mental content; (3) domain-general or domain-specific — some strategies transfer across subjects while others are tied to particular content. Persistence: cognitive strategies endure through explicit instruction in educational settings, through practice and habituation, and through the academic discourse that studies their effectiveness and refines their design. [formal: strategium cognitivum | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.81]

The Internet is a global system of interconnected computer networks that communicates using the TCP/IP protocol suite. Parameters: (1) packet-switched data routing across autonomous systems, (2) standardized protocols (IP for addressing, TCP/UDP for transport, DNS for naming), (3) physical infrastructure of routers, switches, fiber-optic cables, and undersea links. Persistence mechanism: maintained by open standards bodies (IETF, W3C, ICANN) that publish and maintain protocol specifications, combined with the sunk cost of global infrastructure and the network effect — each new connected node increases the value for all existing nodes. The Internet is the made world's central nervous system: not a place, but a protocol family enabling heterogeneous networks to interoperate. [formal: interrete | substrate: matter | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A value proposition is a stated claim specifying what benefit a product or service provides to a particular customer segment, why it is superior to alternatives, and why the customer should pay for it. Parameters: (1) target customer or beneficiary, (2) the core benefit or problem solved, (3) the differentiation from alternatives, (4) the economic rationale for exchange. Persistence mechanism: sustained through marketing, product design, and customer feedback loops — if stated value no longer matches delivered value, the proposition collapses. A value proposition is the bridge between a maker offering and a buyer need, articulated so it can be communicated, tested, and revised. [formal: propositio valoris | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Premeditation is the deliberate advance consideration of future actions and their consequences. It operates through three parameters: (1) temporal displacement — projecting beyond the present moment to simulate outcomes; (2) consequence mapping — linking actions to their predicted effects across time; (3) behavioral inhibition — the capacity to withhold action pending evaluation. Premeditation persists through working memory, prospective simulation, and the meta-cognitive ability to hold multiple futures in mind simultaneously, allowing deliberate choice over impulse. [formal: praemeditatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

gloss is a rhetorical figure in which a word or phrase is followed by an explanation or clarification that restates the original in different terms, often to resolve ambiguity or add nuance. The parameter that carves gloss is the presence of a paired structure: an original term and a glossing term where the second explicates the first without introducing entirely new referential content. Gloss persists through pedagogical transmission — it is taught as a figure of speech in rhetoric curricula and survives in textual commentary traditions where later readers annotate earlier texts to make them intelligible to new audiences. The gloss is not merely decorative; it is a mechanism for preserving interpretive access across temporal and cultural distance. [formal: glossa | substrate: language | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Anaphora is a rhetorical figure of repetition in which the same word or phrase is repeated at the beginning of two or more successive clauses, sentences, or lines. Parameters: (1) the repeated element must be identical or near-identical in form, (2) the repetition must occur at the initial position of each unit, (3) there must be at least two occurrences to constitute the figure. Persistence mechanism: anaphora persists through explicit instruction in rhetorical pedagogy, through written exemplars in literary and oratorical texts, and through performative practice in spoken discourse — it is transmitted across generations by teachers, copied by scribes, and reproduced by speakers who learn the technique. [formal: anaphora | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.98]

A recension is a method of textual criticism in which a scholar compares all available manuscript versions of a text to establish a stemma codicum (family tree of manuscripts) and reconstruct the archetype or most authoritative version. It operates by identifying shared variants, grouping manuscripts into families, and eliminating readings introduced by scribal error, expansion, or abbreviation. The parameters that bound a recension are: (1) the set of extant manuscripts or witnesses being compared, (2) the critical criteria for evaluating variant readings (lectio difficilior, transcriptional probability, genealogical coherence), and (3) the resulting critical text or apparatus that records the editorial reconstruction. A recension persists through the institutional practice of textual scholarship — the teaching of paleographic and philological methods, the production of critical editions, and the ongoing revision of editions when new manuscripts are discovered. It is a cumulative, revisable practice maintained across generations of scholars.\n\n[formal: recensio | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

An oracle is a human institution in which a designated person, object, or site serves as a medium through which a deity or supernatural force is believed to communicate with the living. The oracle produces oracles — authoritative utterances, signs, or inscriptions — that practitioners interpret as guidance, prediction, or revelation. The institution requires: (1) a recognized medium (the pythia at Delphi, the cast lots, the sacred spring); (2) a ritual protocol for consulting the medium (pilgrimage, sacrifice, specific questions); (3) interpretive expertise (priests, seers, augurs who translate the medium's output into actionable counsel); and (4) communal belief in the authority of the oracle's output. The oracle persists through ritual reproduction, textual recording of responses, and the institutional maintenance of the sacred site. Its function is to reduce uncertainty by providing a socially authorized channel for supernatural counsel. [formal: oraculum | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.81]

Commentary is explanatory discourse that interprets, annotates, or analyzes another text, work, or body of knowledge. Its parameters: (1) a primary text or subject that exists independently, (2) a secondary layer of explanation, interpretation, or critique that references the primary, (3) an authorial stance that positions the commentator as mediator between the source and a new audience. Commentary persists through publication, teaching, citation networks, and the institutional practices of scholarship, criticism, and pedagogy — it reproduces each time a reader engages a source through the lens of another's interpretation. [formal: commentarius | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Seduction is a deliberate strategy for winning attraction, compliance, or favor through calculated charm, psychological insight, and performative behavior. It operates by aligning the target's desires with the seducer's aims, using staged reveals, emotional modulation, and role-play rather than force or explicit request. What makes seduction a distinct practice (rather than mere flirting or manipulation) is its architecture of progressive escalation: each successful micro-consent becomes the premise for the next, deeper step. The practice persists through cultural transmission — literature, film, social teaching, and explicit instruction in its techniques — adapting its costume to each era while retaining its core mechanism of desire-alignment.

[formal: seductio | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Implicature is the pragmatic mechanism by which speakers convey meaning beyond the literal content of their utterances, relying on shared conventions, contextual inference, and the listener's capacity to recover intended implications. It operates through conversational maxims (quality, quantity, relation, manner) that listeners use to infer what is meant but not said. The parameters of implicature are: (1) a literal utterance that under-specifies the speaker's intent, (2) shared background assumptions between speaker and listener, (3) an inferential process that bridges the gap, and (4) the distinction between what is said (explicit content) and what is implicated (implicit content). Implicature persists through the teachable rules of conversational inference — the conventions by which communities learn to read between the lines. [formal: implicatura | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: no | epoch: 0.20]

A scholium is a critical commentary or marginal annotation appended to a text, offering explanation, criticism, or contextual notes for readers. Its parameters are: (1) it must reference an existing source text, (2) it provides interpretive or explanatory content distinct from the source, (3) it is structured as an auxiliary note rather than a standalone work. The scholium persists through textual reproduction — copied alongside source texts in manuscripts, printed editions, and digital archives — and through scholarly tradition where commentators build on prior scholia in an accumulating chain of annotation.

[formal: scholium | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.18]

anomaly: A deviation from what a system — statistical, scientific, social, or normative — establishes as expected or normal. Parameters: (1) a baseline or model of normality exists within the system, (2) an observation, object, or event departs from that baseline beyond a defined threshold, (3) the departure is detectable and salient to the system's observers or operators. The concept persists through language, scientific practice, and institutional protocols that flag, catalog, investigate, and sometimes normalize departures from the expected. [formal: anomalia | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.91]

A lemma is a proven mathematical proposition filed not for its own sake but as a stepping stone toward proving a larger, more important result (a proposition or theorem). Its identity is defined by its function: it exists to be used. Parameters: (1) it is itself a completed proof, not a conjecture; (2) its primary purpose is instrumental — to carry a step in a subsequent argument; (3) its name signals to readers that it is auxiliary, not terminal. Persistence: lemmas persist through mathematical literature, being cited, re-cited, and sometimes elevated to proposition or theorem status once their auxiliary role is no longer needed. [formal: lemma | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.42]

Plausibility is a judgment metric that evaluates whether a proposition is coherent enough with existing knowledge to warrant temporary acceptance as a working hypothesis. It carves by three parameters: (1) coherence with background beliefs (not truth, but non-contradiction), (2) available evidence weight (sufficient to support, not prove), and (3) falsifiability threshold (the proposition must be structured so it could fail). Persistence mechanism: plausibility persists through language — it is encoded in epistemic modalities (may, might, could be, probably), in rhetorical framing, and in the disciplinary standards of evidence across fields like science, law, and everyday reasoning. It operates as a gatekeeping filter on belief formation, determining which ideas enter consideration and which are discarded before evaluation. Plausibility is not truth; it is the preliminary pass that lets truth-seeking begin. [formal: plausibilitas | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A judicial act declaring a defendant not guilty of the charged offense. The definition carves a binary outcome (guilty/not guilty) produced by a formal adjudicative process, persisting through institutional record-keeping and the legal doctrine of double jeopardy which prevents re-prosecution on the same charges. It exists as both a written judgment and a social fact: the state acknowledges it cannot prove its case. [formal: acquiesco | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.48]

A supplementary clause or document executed with the same formalities as a will, that adds to, explains, or amends it without revoking the whole. The definition carves a partial-modification instrument: it cannot stand alone (requires the parent will) and cannot contradict the will it modifies (a contradictory codicil operates as a revocation). It persists through testamentary formalities — witnessing, dating, and filing with the probate court — ensuring the testator's final intent is recorded without rewriting. [formal: codicillus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.48]

Etiquette is a system of socially prescribed behavioral rules that govern polite conduct within specific social frames — ceremonies, institutions, social classes, or professional settings. Parameters: (1) the social frame that defines the applicable context, (2) the repertoire of permitted and forbidden actions within that frame, (3) the enforcement mechanism ranging from informal social disapproval to formal ostracism. Persistence mechanism: transmitted through modeling, explicit instruction, and social enforcement — preserved across generations via teaching, ritual practice, and the threat of reputational sanction. [formal: etiquette | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Labeling is the human-made act of attaching a word, symbol, or mark to an object, idea, or category to enable identification, sorting, and communication. Parameters: (1) the label must be a human-created sign — not a natural property; (2) the attachment must be intentional, serving a communicative or organizational function; (3) labels persist through language, writing, digital systems, and social convention. The persistence mechanism is linguistic convention reinforced by repeated use across individuals and institutions. Labels are maps, not territories: a label names a category, it does not constitute the thing categorized. [formal: labellum | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Chronology is the human-made practice of arranging events into a ordered temporal sequence, using calendars, era reckoning, and date notation. Its parameters are: (1) a set of events or phenomena to be ordered, (2) a reference system of units (years, seasons, epochs), (3) a directional convention (before/after, BCE/CE, AD), and (4) a mediation substrate (written records, oral tradition, institutional calendars). It persists through calendrical institutions, written annals, and the teaching of temporal conventions. [formal: chronologia | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.88]

A shelf is a flat, rigid surface mounted to or integrated with a vertical structure (wall, furniture, partition) to hold objects in a static, accessible position. Parameters: (1) the surface must be load-bearing and horizontal or near-horizontal; (2) it must be fixed or semi-fixed, not a portable tray; (3) it operates at one or more discrete levels within a vertical plane. Persistence mechanism: physical manufacture in wood, metal, or composite materials; social persistence through architectural convention and domestic/industrial practice. The shelf extends storage capacity without consuming floor area, converting empty vertical space into usable holding surfaces. [formal: tabula suspendenda | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A family of cryptographic algorithms designed to remain secure against attacks from both classical computers and quantum computers. The defining parameters are: (1) resistance to Shor's algorithm and Grover's algorithm attacks, which threaten RSA, ECC, and symmetric schemes respectively; (2) reliance on mathematical problems believed to be hard even for quantum adversaries — lattice-based, code-based, hash-based, or multivariate polynomial problems; (3) specification through formal security reductions that bound the advantage of any quantum adversary in terms of worst-case hardness of underlying problems. The persistence mechanism is standardization (NIST PQC standardization process), implementation in cryptographic protocols and libraries, and continuous cryptanalytic scrutiny that prunes insecure candidates while validated schemes enter deployment. [formal: cryptographia securitas quantum-nihil | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.23]

A legal mechanism that requires a detaining authority to bring a prisoner before a judge and demonstrate lawful grounds for detention. The defining parameters are: (1) the detained person (or their representative) may invoke it by petition; (2) the detaining authority bears the burden of proving lawful cause; (3) failure to show cause mandates release. The persistence mechanism is constitutional and statutory entrenchment across common-law and civil-law jurisdictions, judicial enforcement through daily court terms, and institutional memory preserved in legal education, procedure codes, and the continuous cycle of petitions and rulings that keep the writ alive as both a right and a procedural requirement. [formal: corpus habendum | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.23]

Entitlement is a socially constructed claim — a representation of what an agent asserts or is recognized as having the right to receive, hold, or do. It operates as a map of claimed right within legal, institutional, and social frameworks. Parameters: (1) source — the entitlement derives from law, custom, contract, or social recognition; (2) strength — ranging from weak social expectation to legally enforceable claim; (3) scope — what goods, behaviors, or treatments are covered. Persistence mechanism: entitlements persist through institutional enforcement (courts, norms, sanctions), social reproduction (teaching, modeling, expectation-setting), and written codification (statutes, contracts, policies). They decay when institutions stop enforcing them, when social consensus shifts, or when codifications are amended.\n\n[formal: titulus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.41]

Tagging is the human practice of attaching labels (tags) to objects, information, or content to enable classification, retrieval, and navigation without requiring a fixed taxonomy. Tags are flexible, user-generated or system-assigned, and can be applied incrementally. The persistence mechanism is language and digital storage: tags survive as metadata strings attached to resources, enabling folksonomic organization that emerges from collective use rather than top-down categorization. [formal: tagging | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.00]

Pragmatics is the study of how context shapes the meaning of language in use. It distinguishes literal, compositional meaning from what speakers actually communicate — implicature, presupposition, speech acts, and the inferential work listeners perform to recover intended meaning. The parameters are: (1) utterance (the spoken or written form), (2) context (situational, cultural, and conversational background), (3) speaker intention (what is meant beyond what is said), and (4) listener inference (the reasoning that bridges said and meant). It persists through linguistic theory, pedagogical practice, and computational natural-language processing systems that model conversational implicature. [formal: pragmatica | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Discovery is the act of finding something that exists independently of the search but is unknown to the discoverer. The parameters are: (1) a pre-existing entity, fact, or phenomenon, (2) a search or investigative process, (3) a knower who previously lacked the knowledge, and (4) the resulting change in the knower's state from ignorance to knowledge. It persists through documentation, communication, and the institutionalization of findings in scientific, historical, or exploratory records. Discovery differs from invention: the thing found was already there; the act of finding is made. [formal: inventio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

precedence is the convention of assigning priority order to competing claims, operations, or entities within a rule system. Its parameters are: (1) a domain of competing items requiring ordering, (2) a ranking criterion — temporal, hierarchical, or lexical — that determines relative position, and (3) a resolution mechanism that breaks ties when criteria conflict. Precedence persists through formal codification: statutes, operator precedence tables, grammatical rules, and scheduling algorithms. It is transmitted by instruction and enforced by institutional practice — a judge applying stare decisis, a compiler resolving expression evaluation, a scheduler choosing among ready processes. [formal: praecedentia | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.93]

A concordance is a structured alphabetical index of every word appearing in a text or corpus, paired with the words immediately preceding and following each occurrence. It carves by three parameters: (1) the word-form granularity (exact lemma vs. all inflectional forms), (2) the context window (how many words appear on each side), and (3) the source boundary (which edition or version of the text constitutes the corpus). The persistence mechanism is publication: the concordance is printed or digitized as a reference work, encoded in a searchable database, and reproduced in subsequent editions with updated entries. Once compiled, it persists as long as its source text survives and someone accesses the indexed form — a tool for navigation through voluminous text without reading it linearly. [formal: concordantia | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.91]

A medium is the intervening substance, channel, or mode through which something is transmitted, accomplished, or expressed. Its parameters are: (1) a source or agent that acts, (2) a target or recipient that receives, and (3) the medium itself as the necessary intermediary that enables the transmission or transformation between them. A medium persists as a conceptual category encoded in language, taught across technical disciplines (physics, art, communications, engineering), and deployed whenever humans need to describe what stands between cause and effect. The medium is not the source nor the target — it is the third term that makes the relation possible. Without the medium, the transmission breaks. [formal: medium | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.48]

A burden is the allocation of responsibility, obligation, or weight across agents. Parameters: (1) the burden-bearer who carries it, (2) the burdened object (proof, care, labor), (3) the weight or measure of obligation. Persistence: language (terms like 'burden of proof', 'burden of care'), law (statutory allocation of responsibility), and social convention (norms of duty). The map divides responsibility into distributable units that can be assigned, transferred, or shared between agents. [formal: onus | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.92]

The entry burden is human-made: it is a convention for distributing obligation across agents, not a natural force. The concept exists through language (the word 'burden' itself), law (burden-of-proof rules), and social practice (who carries what weight). The territory — actual effort or weight — is described but never enrolled.

Scheduling is the practice of allocating actions, events, or resources to specific positions along a time reference, producing an organized sequence that can be followed or consulted. Its parameters are: (1) a set of items to be arranged, (2) a time reference (calendar, duration, order), (3) an allocation rule (priority, constraint, or preference). It persists through externalized representations — written schedules, digital calendars, mental routines — that encode the allocation and allow retrieval and adjustment. The persistence mechanism is the continued accessibility of the schedule artifact, which exists as a mind-independent record (written, digital, or institutional) that survives beyond the act of arranging.\n\n[formal: schedulatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Pedagogy is the systematic practice and study of methods and techniques for teaching and instruction. It carves a distinct domain of human knowledge: not the natural act of transmitting information, but the crafted frameworks, methodologies, and institutionalized approaches that govern how knowledge is deliberately structured and conveyed across generations. Its persistence mechanism is educational tradition, formal teacher training programs, and the accumulated literature of instructional theory that transmits and refines pedagogical methods across communities and epochs. [formal: pedagogia | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Debugging is the systematic process of identifying defects in a human-made artifact, isolating their cause, and applying a correction. It operates as a method of inquiry: the practitioner hypothesizes about the gap between observed behavior and expected behavior, designs tests to narrow the space of possible causes, and verifies that the correction restores intended function. Debugging persists through documented procedures (debuggers, trace logs, bug trackers), taught methods (binary search, rubber-ducking, bisect), and institutional memory (post-mortems, regression suites). Its parameters are: (1) there must be a designed specification to deviate from, (2) the artifact must be inspectable — its state accessible to observation, (3) the process must be repeatable so the fix does not reintroduce the defect. Without a spec, there is nothing to debug; without inspectability, there is only blind trial; without repeatability, the defect is a ghost that returns.

[formal: debuggatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.49]

Analogical reasoning is the human-made cognitive mechanism by which knowledge, structure, or relationships from a known domain (the source) are mapped onto an unfamiliar domain (the target) to infer new properties, generate hypotheses, or solve problems. It operates through three parameters: (1) structural alignment — identifying correspondences between relational elements rather than surface features, (2) mapping — transferring relational knowledge from source to target under constraints of systematicity and one-to-one correspondence, and (3) inference — drawing conclusions about the target that go beyond what is explicitly stated in either domain. The mechanism persists through language (metaphor, analogy, simile as linguistic expressions), education (pedagogical use of familiar examples to teach abstract concepts), and cultural transmission (stories, parables, and case-based reasoning traditions). It is not a natural faculty but a structured method that humans formalize and deploy deliberately — from legal precedent (case law reasoning) to scientific model-building (the planetary model of the atom) to everyday problem-solving (this situation is like that one). [formal: analogia | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.92]

Escrow is a tripartite holding arrangement in which a neutral third party (the escrow agent) retains control of assets, funds, or documents until predefined conditions set by two principal parties are satisfied, at which point the agent releases them to the designated recipient. Parameters: (1) three distinct roles — depositor, beneficiary, and agent; (2) a written escrow agreement specifying conditions and release terms; (3) the agent must hold legal or constructive possession of the escrowed item. The arrangement persists through contractual law, institutional practice of banks and title companies, and the self-enforcing incentive structure: the agent retains control until conditions are verified. Without the agreement and the agent's retained control, the escrow ceases to function. [formal: depositum | substrate: behavior | horizon: a transaction | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.94]

A curriculum is a structured plan for organizing learning content, sequences, and assessments into a coherent program. It specifies what knowledge and skills are to be taught, in what order, and how mastery is measured. Parameters: (1) scope — the domain of knowledge or skills covered; (2) sequence — the order in which topics are presented, progressing from foundational to advanced; (3) assessment — the methods for measuring learner mastery; (4) duration — the time span over which the program operates. Persistence mechanism: curricula persist through institutional codification (syllabi, standards documents), pedagogical tradition (teacher training that transmits the plan), and administrative enforcement (accreditation, grading systems). A curriculum is the map of a learning journey, not the journey itself — it organizes the territory of knowledge for pedagogical traversal.\n\n[curriculum: from Latin currere, to run; the course one runs through knowledge. Substrate: mind. Horizon: a life. Explicit: yes. Epoch: 0.19]

Liability is a human-made construct that assigns responsibility for harm, loss, or obligation to a specific actor or entity. It carves three parameters: (1) the liable party (person, corporation, or entity), (2) the ground of liability (statute, contract, tort, or negligence), and (3) the remedy (damages, injunction, or specific performance). It persists through legal codification, contractual agreement, and social enforcement — a map of accountability that exists wherever human institutions exist to assign blame and allocate loss. [formal: responsabilitas | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.94]

Self-efficacy is the constructed belief that one possesses the capability to organize and execute the courses of action required to manage prospective situations. Parameters: (1) domain-specificity — efficacy beliefs are tied to particular domains rather than global traits, (2) magnitude — the difficulty level of tasks one believes they can handle, (3) strength — the certainty of one's efficacy judgment. Persistence mechanism: sustained through linguistic persuasion, vicarious experience, physiological states, and enactive attainment — all social and psychological practices that propagate the concept through teaching, therapy, and institutional training. [formal: self_efficacia | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.22]

Precommitment is a behavioral strategy whereby an agent deliberately constrains their own future choices to overcome present-bias and time-inconsistent preferences. Parameters: (1) self-constraint enacted at time T1 targeting future behavior at time T2 > T1, (2) motivated by recognition of predictable self-deception or weakness of will, (3) implemented through institutional, technological, or social mechanisms that make deviation costly or impossible. The construct maps a diagnosed failure of temporal self-governance and offers a structural remedy. Persistence mechanism: cultural transmission of institutional designs, behavioral economics frameworks, self-help practices, and legal instruments (e.g., advance directives, automatic savings enrollment). [formal: prae-commisso | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A fiduciary is a person or entity bound by a legally enforceable duty to act solely in the best interest of another party (the beneficiary). The role exists only where law or contract creates it — courts of equity, corporate governance, trust law, and regulated professions (attorneys, trustees, executors, financial advisors) generate and maintain it. The boundary between fiduciary and ordinary commercial actor is drawn by the presence of a duty of loyalty, care, and good faith that outranks self-interest. Persistence mechanism: legal precedent, statutory codification, and professional licensing bodies enforce the standard through sanctions and remediation.

[formal: fīduciārius | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.94]

A taxonomy-of-tasks is a structured classification system that groups human activities by shared attributes: cognitive demand level, required skill sets, output modality, and temporal structure. Its parameters are the classification dimensions (e.g. physical-vs-mental, routine-vs-novel) and the hierarchy depth. It persists through institutional use in curriculum design, occupational classification standards, and organizational workflow documentation. [formal: taxonomia officiorum | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A stereotype is a standardized mental category that maps a social group onto a fixed set of attributes, operating as a cognitive shortcut that sacrifices individual variation for predictive ease. Parameters: (1) the group must be socially recognized as a boundary; (2) the attribute set must be treated as necessary rather than accidental by the holder; (3) the category persists through repetition in discourse, institutional practice, and pedagogical transmission. Stereotypes are human-made because they are learned constructs — they do not exist in nature but are produced and maintained by social systems of classification and narrative. [formal: stereotupum | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Representativeness is the human-made cognitive construct for judging the probability or frequency of an event by how closely it resembles a typical case or prototype, ignoring base rates and statistical independence. Parameters: (1) similarity-based judgment, (2) neglect of base rates, (3) neglect of sample size, (4) insensitivity to predictability. The construct persists through teaching in statistics and psychology, through naming (heuristics-and-biases literature), and through repeated disciplinary use in diagnosing systematic error. [formal: representativitas | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Reflection is the structured cognitive practice of deliberately examining one's own thoughts, actions, decisions, or knowledge to extract meaning and improve future performance. Parameters: (1) requires conscious attention directed inward at one's own mental states; (2) involves systematic re-examination, not casual rumination; (3) produces explicit insights or behavioral adjustments. Persistence mechanism: maintained through disciplined practice, documented in pedagogical traditions (Sch\u00f6n's reflective practice), and institutionalized in learning frameworks (Kolb's experiential learning cycle). [formal: reflectio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.12]

Anchoring is the cognitive bias wherein an initial value — presented as a number, standard, or reference point — exerts disproportionate influence on subsequent judgments and estimates, even when the anchor is arbitrary or irrelevant. The mechanism operates through two paths: selective accessibility (the anchor primes related information in memory) and adjustment insufficiency (subjects start from the anchor but fail to adjust far enough to reach the true value). Anchoring persists across expertise domains, ages cultures, and manifests in pricing negotiations, legal sentencing, medical diagnosis, and probabilistic forecasting. Its persistence mechanism is language and teaching — anchored frames propagate through instruction, precedent, and repeated exposure to the same reference points. [formal: anchoring | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.13]

Folk-psychology is the human-made conceptual framework for attributing mental states — beliefs, desires, intentions, fears, and goals — to oneself and other agents. Its parameters are: (1) the attribution of unobservable inner states to explain observable behaviour; (2) the assumption that agents act rationally given their beliefs and desires; (3) the predictive function of inferring future actions from ascribed mental states. It persists through language (verbs like 'believe', 'want', 'think'), social teaching (theory-of-mind training in development), and cultural narratives (stories, moral judgments, legal attribution of intent). It is not the natural cognitive capacity to read minds — humans have no such capacity — but the map built to approximate it. [formal: philosophia vulgaris | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.98]

Proportionality is the normative principle that a response, classification, or constraint should be scaled to match the gravity of its cause — the offense, the risk, or the evidence. It carves three parameters: (1) the stimulus (act, threat, or fact), (2) the response (sanction, measure, or judgment), and (3) the scaling rule (balance, equivalence, or necessity) that connects them. Without any one parameter the concept collapses: no stimulus means no trigger, no response means nothing to calibrate, no scaling rule means brute force or whim. Proportionality persists through legal codification (statutes, constitutions, case law), ethical teaching (utilitarian and deontological frameworks), and institutional practice (sentencing guidelines, use-of-force policies). It is a standard of review as much as a rule — judges weigh proportionality; institutions design for it. [formal: proportio | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.01]

Procedural-memory is the human-made psychological category for the class of long-term memory that stores motor skills, habits, and automatic procedures. It is defined in opposition to declarative memory (facts and events), characterized by implicit, non-conscious retention that persists even when explicit recall is impaired. The category was introduced by Squire and colleagues in the 1980s to carve a functional distinction in cognitive architecture. Persistence mechanism: academic discipline, teaching, and the accumulated corpus of cognitive science literature. [formal: memoria proceduralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.16]

Dual-process theory is the human-made cognitive science framework that posits two distinct modes of information processing: System 1, which operates automatically, rapidly, and without conscious effort; and System 2, which operates slowly, deliberately, and with effortful computation. The parameters that define it are: (a) two dissociable processing modes, (b) differing speed, effort, and awareness, (c) potential conflict between systems resolved by System 2 overriding System 1. It persists through the mechanism of academic institutionalization — peer-reviewed research programs, textbook pedagogy, and experimental paradigms that reproduce and test the model across decades of cognitive psychology. [formal: duplex-processus | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A script is a cognitive schema encoding the expected sequence of events, roles, and actions in a recurrent situation type (e.g., dining at a restaurant, attending a classroom). It is a human-made mental structure — not the events themselves but the organized prediction framework that enables automatic recognition and guided participation. Parameters: (1) situation-type identifies the class of events the script covers, (2) role assignments specify expected actor positions, (3) event-chains enumerate the canonical sequence, (4) props and settings enumerate required objects and environments. Persistence mechanism: scripts persist through language (stories, instructions, socialization), institutional teaching (onboarding, training, ritual rehearsal), and cultural transmission across generations. They are activated by situational cues and operate largely outside conscious awareness until violated, at which point they trigger error-correction and conscious attention. [formal: scriptum | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: no | epoch: 0.15]

Skepticism is a human-made epistemic discipline that institutionalizes doubt as a method of inquiry. It carves a practiced stance: systematically withholding assent from propositions until sufficient evidence and reasoning standards are met. Its parameters are (1) a method of questioning rather than a conclusion of disbelief, (2) a set of criteria for evidentiary thresholds that vary by domain (scientific, philosophical, legal), and (3) a social practice embedded in institutions such as peer review, cross-examination, and falsification protocols. Skepticism persists through educational traditions, institutionalized review processes, and rhetorical conventions that train practitioners to suspend judgment — it is taught, not innate. The map of skepticism is not the natural faculty of caution but the cultivated practice of methodological doubt, codified in disciplines from Cartesian doubt to scientific skepticism.\n\n[formal: skeptical method | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.47]

Confirmation bias is a human-made cognitive taxonomy — a named pattern in how human agents selectively process information. It carves a class of systematic error: the tendency to seek, interpret, favor, and recall information in ways that confirm preexisting beliefs while giving disproportionate weight to disconfirming evidence. Its parameters are (1) directional information search (actively seeking confirming evidence), (2) interpretive asymmetry (ambiguity resolved toward existing beliefs), (3) memory distortion (selective recall of confirming instances), and (4) persistence mechanism: it is tracked and measured through experimental psychology protocols (e.g., Wason selection task, belief-bias paradigm), named in diagnostic frameworks, and mitigated by institutional practices like blind review, pre-registration, and structured analytic techniques. The entry denotes the MAP of the phenomenon — the conceptual category and its measurement tools — not the natural cognitive tendency itself (Law 2a). It persists through research literatures, diagnostic criteria, and trained awareness practices.\n\n[formal: partisanship in cognition | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.47]

Apparatus is a human-made arrangement of interconnected components designed to perform a function that no single component could achieve alone. It carves three parameters: (1) structural integration — parts bound by a shared design logic so they operate as a unified system, (2) functional emergence — the collective capacity exceeds the sum of individual parts (a telescope does not merely contain lenses; it enables vision at distances no eye can reach), and (3) persistence through institutionalized manufacture, maintenance protocols, and operational training. Apparatus persists via technical documentation, maintenance schedules, and the social practices of assembly and calibration. It is always a constructed artifact — not the natural world it may study or manipulate, but the human-built scaffold that extends human capability. The apparatus of science, for instance, is not nature itself but the instruments, protocols, and institutions built to interrogate it.\n\n[formal: apparatus | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.47]

Fade is the human-made concept of gradual diminution — the deliberate or observed process by which something loses presence, intensity, or salience across a defined span. It carves three parameters: (1) the fading entity (a signal, memory, social practice, or physical artifact), (2) the rate of loss (continuous or stepwise), and (3) the endpoint (total disappearance, asymptotic threshold, or reversible state). Fade persists as a named category in art, rhetoric, technology, and everyday discourse; it is the map of diminution that humans construct to track, anticipate, and sometimes engineer the waning of presence. [formal: fade | substrate: mind | horizon: hours|a life|a generation | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.16]

The default-effect is the human-made concept of the systematic tendency to prefer pre-selected or status-quo options when presented with a choice set. It is a category from behavioral economics and choice architecture that describes how the placement of an option as the default rather than any intrinsic quality of that option increases its selection rate above alternatives. The mechanism operates through loss aversion, endowment effects, and social signals. The boundary applies only when a default is explicitly set by a choice architect, not to options that happen to appear first. Persistence mechanism: established through peer-reviewed research in behavioral economics, codified in behavioral insights teams across governments, embedded in commercial choice-design frameworks, and taught in psychology and economics curricula. [formal: defaultis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Due diligence is the human-made practice of conducting systematic investigation, verification, and analysis before entering an agreement, acquisition, or undertaking. It carves a bounded process: scope the subject, gather and assess evidence, identify risks and liabilities, and produce a documented assessment. Persistence mechanism: professional standards, regulatory requirements, and institutional memory encode the practice across transactions and jurisdictions, ensuring it persists as a required step in high-stakes decision-making. [formal: diligentia praevia | substrate: behavior | horizon: a transaction | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.94]

Scaffolding is a pedagogical technique in which temporary, adjustable support is provided to a learner to enable performance beyond their independent capability, with the support gradually withdrawn as competence increases. Parameters: (1) the support structure — examples, prompts, modeling, or tools supplied by an instructor or peer; (2) the fading schedule — the rate at which support is reduced as the learner gains independence; (3) the competence threshold — the point at which the learner can perform the task unaided and the scaffold is removed. Persistence mechanism: transmitted through teaching practice, teacher training programs, and educational literature; maintained as a standing concept in instructional design and cognitive science. [formal: subsidium | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.16]

Due process is the legal practice of following fair and established procedures before depriving a person of life, liberty, or property. It requires notice, hearing, and impartial adjudication as conditions of any governmental action affecting individual rights. It persists through codified statutes, constitutional provisions, and judicial precedent that bind administrative and judicial actors to standardized procedure. [formal: due_process | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.50]

belief-bias is the tendency to evaluate arguments by the believability of their conclusions rather than by their logical validity. When an argument has a plausible conclusion, people accept its reasoning as strong; when the conclusion is implausible, the same reasoning is judged weak. The parameters of the effect are: (1) separation of conclusion believability from argument validity, (2) the conflict condition where valid arguments have implausible conclusions and invalid arguments have plausible conclusions, and (3) the measure of bias as the accuracy gap between believable and unbelievable valid arguments. It persists through metacognitive training (the explicit practice of separating conclusion truth from argument structure), logical literacy education, and the habitual application of formal analysis to evaluative judgment. [formal: bias credulitatis | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: no | epoch: 0.48]

framing-effect is the phenomenon by which the same objective information produces different judgments or choices depending on how it is presented — as a gain or as a loss, as a survival rate or mortality rate, as a cost or as a savings. The parameters are: (1) value equivalence between frames (the described outcomes are identical in magnitude), (2) valence shift in presentation (gain vs. loss frame), and (3) directional asymmetry (loss frames elicit risk-seeking, gain frames elicit risk-aversion). It persists through the architecture of human language and communication — the inescapability of some presentation over another — and through the design of decision environments (nudges, disclosures, default options) that exploit framing by making one frame dominant. [formal: effectus framingis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.48]

Dual-process-theory is a human-made theoretical framework that models human cognition as operating through two distinct and interacting systems. System 1 processes information rapidly, automatically, and without conscious effort — relying on heuristics, pattern recognition, and associative memory. System 2 processes information slowly, deliberately, and with conscious effort — applying logical reasoning, rule-following, and working memory. The parameters of the theory are: (1) two systems with different processing speeds and capacities, (2) each system operates independently but can interact, (3) System 1 defaults to automatic processing while System 2 requires activation and effort, (4) the interaction between systems explains cognitive biases when System 1 heuristics override System 2 reasoning. The theory persists through peer-reviewed research literature in cognitive psychology and behavioral economics, formal teaching in university courses, and operationalization in experimental paradigms that measure response times, error rates, and neurophysiological markers. [formal: dualis processus theoriam | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Negligence is the failure to exercise the degree of care that the law requires a reasonable person to exercise in given circumstances. It has three parameters: (1) a duty of care owed by the defendant to the plaintiff, (2) breach of that duty through act or omission falling below the reasonable standard, and (3) resulting damage causally linked to the breach. The persistence mechanism is judicial precedent — each ruling refines the reasonable-person standard and extends or limits the scope of duty. [formal: negligentia | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.94]

A meme is a unit of cultural information — a pattern, idea, behavior, or style — that spreads from one mind to another within a culture through imitation and communication. The parameters of a meme include: (1) a replicable content (a tune, a phrase, a fashion, a belief), (2) a transmission vector (speech, writing, media, observation), and (3) a retention mechanism (memory, recording, ritual). Memes persist through the substrate of language and human teaching — without these, they cannot replicate. The concept carves a class of culturally transmitted units distinguished by their replicative behavior rather than their content. [formal: meme | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The abstraction-ladder is a human-made conceptual model that organizes levels of specificity from concrete particulars at the bottom to abstract categories at the top. Each rung represents a level of generalization: moving upward, details are dropped in favor of shared properties; moving downward, distinguishing features are added. The model was invented by Alfred Korzybski as a teaching and thinking tool to help users notice when they are conflating different levels of abstraction (the classic error of treating a category as identical to one of its instances). Its persistence mechanism is pedagogical: taught in critical thinking, linguistics, and philosophy curricula, used in cognitive psychology and knowledge representation, and invoked in everyday discourse to diagnose categorical reasoning errors. [formal: scala abtractionum | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Gamification is the practice of applying game-design elements — such as points, badges, leaderboards, challenges, levels, and progress feedback — to non-game contexts (education, workplace, health, marketing) to motivate participation, increase engagement, and shape behavior. Its parameters are: (1) game mechanics borrowed from game design, (2) deployment in a non-game context, and (3) an intentional behavioral or engagement goal. It persists through digital platforms that implement these mechanics, through organizational policies and practices, and through the cultural diffusion of game-like engagement patterns across sectors. [formal: gamificatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Sarcasm is a figure of speech in which words are deployed to convey the opposite of their literal meaning, typically for humor, irony, or social criticism. Parameters: (1) utterance — a statement whose surface meaning contradicts the intended meaning, (2) context — shared knowledge between speaker and listener that signals the reversal, (3) intent — the speaker's aim to signal incongruity rather than deceive. Persistence mechanism: sarcasm persists through the conventions of pragmatic language use, taught implicitly in language acquisition and explicitly in literary and rhetorical education, sustained by the social practice of reading between the lines. [formal: sarcasmus | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: no | epoch: 0.18]

A caution is a human-made legal construct in which a party deposits money, property, or other security to guarantee the performance of an obligation or the fulfillment of a specified condition. Its parameters are: (1) the deposit — a quantifiable sum or asset held in escrow or pledge; (2) the secured obligation — the specific act, payment, or condition whose performance the deposit guarantees; (3) the forfeiture and return rules — the conditions under which the deposit is retained by the beneficiary or returned to the depositor. The caution persists through statutory frameworks, contractual clauses, and institutional enforcement mechanisms that define its terms and adjudicate disputes. [formal: cautio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A pun is a linguistic device that deliberately exploits the ambiguity of words — their multiple meanings, homophony, or similar sound — to produce a humorous or rhetorical effect. The parameters are: (1) a word or phrase with at least two interpretable meanings, (2) a context that invites one reading while the other is activated for comic or rhetorical surprise, (3) the listener's recognition of both readings. Pun persists through language: it lives in speech, writing, and the cultural practice of wordplay that is taught and transmitted socially. [formal: punitas | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Meta-cognition is the human-made conceptual framework for thinking about one's own thinking — the deliberate, explicit tracking and regulation of cognitive processes. It carves a second-order map: not thought itself, but the organized practice of monitoring, evaluating, and adjusting how thought operates. Parameters include (1) awareness of one's own cognitive state, (2) deliberate regulation of that state (e.g., choosing strategies, checking for errors, reallocating attention), and (3) the ability to reflect on the reliability of one's own judgments. It persists through structured educational practices (metacognitive instruction), self-report instruments, and formalized training protocols in psychology, education, and cognitive science — disciplines that codify and transmit these practices across generations. [formal: meta-cognitio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Optimism bias is the human-made psychological construct describing the systematic tendency for individuals to believe they are less likely than others to experience negative events and more likely than others to experience positive events. It carves a specific error-pattern in probabilistic self-assessment: not general positive affect, but a quantifiable deviation in risk-benefit estimation where personal outcomes are judged more favorably than base-rate statistics warrant. Parameters include (1) comparative risk judgment (self vs. others), (2) domain generality (health, finance, safety, career), and (3) asymmetric valuation (downweighting threats, upweighting opportunities). It persists through empirical measurement in behavioral economics and social psychology, clinical assessment protocols, and public health communication frameworks that identify and correct for its effects. [formal: optimismia bias | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: no | epoch: 0.02]

Hegemony is the human-made political concept describing a form of social power in which a dominant group secures the voluntary compliance of subordinate groups not through coercion but through the cultural and ideological control of meaning — the shaping of common sense so that the dominant group's interests appear as the natural, universal order. It carves a mechanism of power that operates beneath force: the production of consent through institutions (education, media, religion, law) that define what counts as normal, reasonable, and inevitable. Parameters include (1) the institutional channels through which dominant narratives are disseminated, (2) the internalization of these narratives by subordinated groups, and (3) the exclusion or marginalization of alternative framings. It persists through the reproduction of educational curricula, media ownership structures, and the institutionalization of specific worldviews as professional knowledge. [formal: hegemonia | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.03]

Hysteresis is the human-made analytical concept describing a system's dependence on its history: when the output state at any time depends not only on the current inputs but on the sequence of past inputs, producing lag, memory effects, and path-dependent behavior. Parameters: (1) path-dependence — the trajectory matters, not just endpoints; (2) irreversibility — returning inputs to their original values does not restore the original state; (3) hysteresis loop — the distinct forward and return paths form a closed curve in state space. Persistence mechanism: mathematical modeling, scientific education, and cross-domain terminology (physics, economics, materials science, psychology, engineering) carry the concept as a shared analytical framework. [formal: hysteresis | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Noticing is the human-made concept of intentional attentional selection within the mind. Parameters: (1) stimulus filtering — the deliberate selection of specific signals from a broader perceptual field; (2) attentional allocation — the directed deployment of cognitive resources toward chosen inputs; (3) signal detection — the reliable identification of target phenomena against background noise. Persistence mechanism: trained through deliberate practice, pedagogical exercises, and attentional discipline — the map persists as a teachable skill that varies in reliability across cultures and training regimes. [formal: notitia | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.00]

Catechism is a human-made pedagogical construct: a method of instruction structured as a systematic sequence of questions and answers, designed for memorization, doctrinal transmission, and behavioral formation. Parameters: (1) interrogative structure — organized Q&A format where each question targets a specific proposition; (2) cumulative architecture — questions build from simple to complex in a fixed order; (3) memorization requirement — the answers are expected to be committed to memory verbatim; (4) authority channel — the content carries institutional authority, originating from religious teaching traditions and deployable in secular training contexts. Persistence mechanism: catechisms endure through institutional teaching practice (religious education, military training, political indoctrination), canonical written texts (catechisms as books), and ritualized recitation — the method persists wherever institutions reproduce it through structured Q&A drills. [formal: catechismus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.18]

Cognitive-mapping is the human-made concept of an internal mental representation of external spatial or relational structure — a model constructed by humans to describe how organisms organize navigational, categorical, or conceptual knowledge. The parameters are: (1) it is a representational construct, not the navigational act itself; (2) it maps relations between entities (places, categories, ideas) rather than recording sensory detail; (3) it serves as a guide to behavior — planning routes, inferring shortcuts, reorganizing after change. The concept persists through cognitive science, psychology, and geography, where it is taught, measured via tasks like the Corsi block-tapping test or Latour-based map drawing, and refined across research programs from Tolman's latent learning to modern spatial cognition. [formal: cognitivism spatialis | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: no | epoch: 0.17]

Footwear is the human-made category of protective and decorative garments designed to cover and shield the feet. It is defined by three parameters: (1) function — protection, support, or adornment of the foot; (2) construction — the joining of materials (leather, rubber, fabric, synthetic polymers) into a form shaped for the human foot; and (3) cultural norm — social rules governing when, where, and what type of footwear is appropriate. Footwear persists through manufacturing traditions, design canon, retail systems, and the everyday practice of dressing — people make, buy, wear, and discard footwear continuously across all societies. [formal: calceamentum | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Cognitive load is the human-made model that treats working memory as a finite resource consumed by information processing tasks. The theory carves three parameters: intrinsic load (complexity inherent to the material), extraneous load (poorly designed presentation that wastes capacity), and germane load (effort devoted to building schemas). It persists through educational design frameworks, human-factors engineering, and instructional technology that measure, partition, and minimize load to improve learning outcomes. The model persists as a quantitative lens applied to any learning or decision environment where bandwidth constraints are assumed to affect performance. [formal: cognitum onus | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Priming is the human-made experimental paradigm and theoretical construct describing how prior exposure to a stimulus influences the response to a subsequent stimulus, without conscious awareness of the influence. Three parameters carve the phenomenon: semantic priming (related concepts speed processing), perceptual priming (form repetition aids recognition), and affective priming (mood states bias subsequent evaluations). Priming persists through social psychology research programs, marketing and advertising practices, and behavioral economics models that exploit unconscious cueing. Its persistence rests on a vast literature of repetition-effects and a mechanism — latent activation spreading through associative networks — that makes the concept applicable to any domain where prior experience shapes subsequent judgment. [formal: praeparatio | substrate: mind | horizon: moments | explicit: no | epoch: 0.01]

Abductive reasoning is the human-made model of inference to the best explanation: generating a hypothesis that, if true, would account for an observed phenomenon. It carves three parameters: the explanatory gap (observed data lacking a sufficient existing explanation), the hypothesis space (candidate explanations ranked by plausibility), and the selection criterion (inference to the explanation with the highest explanatory power, simplicity, and coherence with background knowledge). Abductive reasoning persists through scientific methodology, diagnostic practice in medicine, detective work, and machine-learning pattern recognition. It occupies the logical space between deduction (guaranteed conclusions from premises) and induction (generalizing from instances), serving as the creative engine of discovery that proposes new theories for later testing. [formal: abductio | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Epistemic humility is the human-made disposition to recognize and acknowledge the limits of one's knowledge, beliefs, and cognitive reach. It carves a cultivated virtue — not the natural state of ignorance, but a reflective stance toward one's own fallibility. Parameters: (1) awareness of cognitive limits, (2) willingness to revise beliefs in light of counterevidence, (3) openness to alternative perspectives. It persists through philosophical teaching, Socratic dialogue, scientific practice, and discursive culture. [formal: humilitas epistemica | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

friction is the resistance that arises in social and institutional processes when participants must expend extra effort — time, attention, or resources — to complete an action that could otherwise proceed directly. It is human-made through the accumulation of requirements, permissions, protocols, and mismatches between systems: identity checks, formatting rules, jurisdictional boundaries, and interface incompatibilities. Friction persists through formalization (codified procedures that encode past decisions into present constraints) and through path dependence (systems that layer new requirements atop older ones without removing obsolete ones). It is studied and managed in design, organizational theory, and behavioral economics as a deliberate or incidental property of systems that must balance efficiency against verification, safety, and control. [formal: frictio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.18]

The concept of awareness is the human-made category for conscious recognition — the map of subjective experience that distinguishes mere processing from felt presence. It is not the natural phenomenon of consciousness (that is territory); it is the framework humans built — through language, introspection practices, and disciplines like phenomenology, cognitive science, and philosophy of mind — to pick out, discuss, and train patterns of recognition. Parameters: (1) the subject must be capable of representing its own relation to what it recognizes — not mere stimulus-response, (2) the map varies across cultures and disciplines — Western phenomenology, Eastern contemplative traditions, and analytic philosophy each carve the territory differently. The awareness-concept persists through vocabulary and taxonomies of consciousness, through trained introspective practices that refine what can be noticed, and through academic study that debates and expands the category's boundaries. [formal: conscientia | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: no | epoch: 0.01]

A checksum is the human-made construct of a fixed-size value derived from a data sequence by a deterministic algorithm, used to verify data integrity. Parameters: (1) digest — a short, fixed-length string produced by a hash or checksumming algorithm applied to input data of arbitrary length; (2) comparison — a mechanism to detect modification by re-computing the digest and matching it against a stored or transmitted value; (3) collision-resistance — the property that finding two distinct inputs producing the same digest is computationally infeasible (for cryptographic checksums). Persists via encoding in file headers, network packets, software distributions, and storage systems as a standard integrity check. [formal: checksum | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Epistemic rationality is the human-made concept of evaluating and updating beliefs in accordance with evidence and probabilistic reasoning. Its parameters are: (1) a norm of belief alignment with available evidence, (2) a mechanism for belief revision when new evidence arrives, and (3) a distinction between epistemic rationality (truth-tracking) and instrumental rationality (goal-achievement). The construct persists through disciplines that operationalize it — epistemology, cognitive psychology, the Bayesian reasoning framework, and scientific methodology — transmitted via teaching and debated in philosophical and scientific literature. [formal: rationalitas epistemica | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Reasoning bias is the human-made concept describing systematic departures from rational or objective reasoning in human cognition. Its parameters are: (1) predictable directional deviation from logical norms, (2) origin in cognitive heuristics or motivational processes, and (3) classification taxonomy (cognitive biases, motivational biases, social biases).
